summary: Write the missing collocation scripts, then review drafts four at a time, returning field edits

edits.value: mou kaerina yo. shigoto wa ashita!
edits.why: Heard right after Mai's cat-food line, 'sore wa ashita' most naturally points to the shopping (do it tomorrow), which clashes with lines 13-15. Naming the work removes the ambiguity the gist relies on.

edits.value: もう帰りなよ。仕事は明日！
edits.why: Kept in step with the romaji change: the work, not the shopping, waits till tomorrow.

edits.value: もうかえりなよ。しごとはあした！
edits.why: Kept in step with the romaji change.

edits.value: Just go home already. The work can wait till tomorrow!
edits.why: The English 'That can wait' had the same ambiguity. It now matches the new line.

edits.value: shigoto | 仕事 | work, your job (shigoto wa ashita = the work can wait till tomorrow)
edits.why: shigoto is new in line 11 and is not a stage-1 word.

edits.value: Line 2: Mai expects to be home late again (kyou mo kaeri osoku naru naa). Line 9: Yuki suggests stepping out (chotto soto ni deyou yo), which reminds Mai that she has to go shopping because she's out of cat food (line 10: kaimono ni ikanai to. neko no gohan, mou nai n da). Yuki tells her to go home and leave the work till tomorrow (line 11: mou kaerina yo. shigoto wa ashita!), Mai agrees (line 12: kyou wa mou uchi ni kaeru!), and Yuki says she'll come shopping too and asks to come over (line 13). A is wrong: Mai doesn't stay, and Yuki goes shopping with her, not for her (kaimono, watashi mo iku yo). B is wrong: they never step out for food and come back. The work waits till tomorrow (line 11), and Mai goes home.
edits.why: Quotes the revised line 11.

edits.value: Line 9: soto ni deru is getting out of the building, and chotto makes it just for a bit. Yuki says it right after Mai admits she hasn't stepped outside all day (line 7: soto ni mo detenai no? / line 8: detenai yo), and adds that the rain has stopped (ame mo yanda shi). B is wrong: going home is kaeru, and Yuki only tells her to go home later, in line 11 (mou kaerina yo), once Mai remembers the cat food. C reads it as English 'go out' for an evening out. soto ni deru only means stepping outside, and chotto keeps it short.
edits.why: The old text said Yuki only uses kaeru later, in line 11. But she says it in line 1 (mada kaeranai no?), and the question 2 explanation cites that line, so the two explanations contradicted each other.

edits.value: In the first call, Yuki offers to drive to the station, and her mother turns her down. What did her mother say?
edits.why: This happens twice: line 5 leads to line 6, and line 11 leads to line 12 (ii no, ii no...). Without naming the call, the cue fits both moments, and a listener who remembers the second refusal finds no matching choice.

edits.value: kaze dete kita ne. daijoubu?
edits.why: Heard on its own, 'kaze, daijoubu?' is the stock phrase for 'How's your cold?' (風邪). 'kaze dete kita ne' (the wind's picking up) is what a friend would actually say, and it can only mean wind.

edits.value: 風出てきたね。大丈夫？
edits.why: Matches the revised romaji cue.

edits.value: かぜでてきたね。だいじょうぶ？
edits.why: Matches the revised romaji cue.

edits.value: It's a warm evening, and you and Kenta are sitting by the river when a breeze picks up. He says, "kaze dete kita ne. daijoubu?" (It's getting breezy. You okay?) Tell him you're fine: it feels nice.
edits.why: The prompt quotes the cue, so it has to change with it.

edits.value: iu | 言う | say (nan to iimashita ka = what did they say?)
edits.why: Two spoken question cues use iu (iimashita ka), and iu isn't a Stage 1 word. Scripts 6, 8 and 9 list it; this script left it out.

edits.value: Line 5: mada mitenai means 'I haven't seen it yet'. The -te nai form with mada says it hasn't happened so far. Line 6 confirms the plan: Sora asks hon yonde kara eiga miru no? (So you'll read the book, then see the film?) and she says un. A is wrong: she does mean to see it, once she's read the book; 'I'm not going to watch it' would be minai. And don't say mada minai for 'I haven't watched it', the usual slip for English speakers: plain -nai with mada is a decision ('I'm not watching it yet'), not a report. C is wrong because Mai says uun (no). Sora is the one who has seen it, yesterday (line 4: kinou mita n da).
edits.why: The old explanation said choice A ('she isn't going to watch it; the book is enough') is close to mada minai. But mada minai means 'not watching it yet', a plan to watch later, so it doesn't match A at all and confuses the teaching point.

edits.value: A rainy Saturday afternoon at the café where Sora works. There are no other customers, so he has been singing behind the counter. Mai, a regular, sits nearby with a book.
edits.why: The setting says there are no customers and then puts Mai, a regular customer, in the café.

edits.value: Time is something there is or isn't, so it's jikan ga nai, not jikan o motte nai. Kenta says it to himself in lines 1 and 17 (jikan nai!) and politely to Satou-san in line 3 (ima chotto jikan ga nai n desu). It's about right now, so use jikan, not hima: hima ga nai means no free time these days (line 5). Mou jikan nai! means 'I'm out of time!'. With a friend, drop ga and end with n da.
edits.why: The explanation says Kenta says 'mou jikan nai' in line 17, but he actually says 'mou hachiji juppun! jikan nai!' The phrase isn't in the transcript.

edits.value: iu | 言う | say (nan to iimashita ka? = what did he say?)
edits.why: Iu (Stage 2) is heard in the 'heard' question (nan to iimashita ka?) but has no gloss. Scripts 11-13 list it for the same question.

edits.value: ofuro haitte ii yo.
edits.why: A younger brother wouldn't call his big sister by her bare name, and Kenji says neechan in every other script. Dropping the name keeps the line natural without adding a new word.

edits.value: お風呂入っていいよ。
edits.why: Matches the romaji change (Kenji no longer calls his big sister 'Yuki').

edits.value: おふろはいっていいよ。
edits.why: Matches the romaji change (Kenji no longer calls his big sister 'Yuki').

edits.value: You can get in the bath now.
edits.why: Matches the romaji change (Kenji no longer calls his big sister 'Yuki').

edits.value: osoi | 遅い | late, slow (osoi yo! = you took ages!)
edits.why: Osoi (Stage 3) is used in line 12 (osoi yo!), but it isn't a target, a review word or a new word.

edits.value: shawaa abite, hige kezutte, ha migaite.
edits.why: The old wrong choice, 'kao aratte', is just as natural there as the right answer, which breaks the heard-question rule. Kezuru is the dictionary 'shave' (wood, a pencil), a real trap for an English speaker, and it's clearly wrong for a beard.

edits.value: Showering, shaving down my beard, brushing my teeth.
edits.why: Gloss for the new wrong choice, hige kezutte.

edits.value: Line 13: hige sotte. soru means shaving hair off with a razor, and in line 14 Yuki repeats it to tease him (hige sotta no? doko ni hige aru no?). B is what English 'cut' leads to, but hige o kiru means trimming a beard with scissors, not shaving it off. C is the dictionary trap: kezuru is the 'shave' of shaving wood or a pencil down, and it's never used for hair. Stubble and beards are always soru.
edits.why: Rewritten to explain the new wrong choice C (kezuru instead of kao aratte).

edits.value: kezuru | 削る | shave down, whittle (wood, a pencil); never used for hair
edits.why: The new wrong choice uses kezuru. Script 12 does the same thing: it glosses kiru (wear), a word that appears only in a wrong choice.

edits.value: asobi ni iku is also the everyday way to say you'll visit someone's place. In line 14 Yuki's mother says yuki no uchi ni asobi ni iku ne (I'll come over to your place), and in line 16 hachiji ni iku kara ne (I'll be there at eight). Kenta says kuru because you'd be coming to him, but you answer from where you are, so it's iku. English 'I'll come over' tempts asobi ni kuru, but that would mean Kenta is the one coming. Don't let English 'play' make asobi sound childish: adults say asobi ni iku all the time, for a visit like this or a fun day out. iku iku is the eager yes Yuki gives in line 13.
edits.why: The draft says asobu on its own 'sounds like kids playing', which is false (adults say kondo asobou, as the brief notes) and turns the brief's trap upside down.

edits.value: un, eigo wa chotto dake hanaseru yo.
edits.why: Model answer 1 drops eigo, so it practises only hanaseru and not the target eigo o hanasu. eigo wa chotto dake hanaseru is the brief's own natural phrasing.

edits.value: うん、英語はちょっとだけ話せるよ。
edits.why: Keeps ja in step with the romaji fix, so the model answer contains the target collocation.

edits.value: Yeah, I can speak a little English.
edits.why: The English now matches the revised model answer, which names English.

edits.value: Say you can speak a little English, with hanasu in its can-form: un, eigo wa chotto dake hanaseru yo.
edits.why: The answer quotes model answer 1, so it has to match the revised wording that includes eigo.

edits.value: The everyday tummy ache is onaka ga itai, usually onaka itai in casual talk, as in Kenji's line 4 (onaka itai) and Okaasan's line 5 (onaka itai no?). The dictionary word i (stomach) is heard too (i ga itai), but onaka is the everyday word, and the natural one at the table. N da makes it the reason you've stopped eating. The second model answers the daijoubu? part, the way Kenji does in line 6 (daijoubu ja nai).
edits.why: The draft says i (stomach) 'belongs to medical talk', which is inaccurate: i ga itai is common in everyday speech, as the brief's trap says.

edits.value: jaa, futari, tomodachi ni shita no?
edits.why: Mai says tomodachi dekita in the very next line (17), answering this question, so choice B was said in the audio and is a fair inference from her reply. That breaks the heard rule. It is replaced with a 'make' calque (ni suru) that nobody says.

edits.value: So, did you two make someone your friend?
edits.why: Gloss for the new choice B (tomodachi ni suru = turn someone into your friend).

edits.value: Line 16: Yuki asks whether the two of them have become friends with each other, so it's tomodachi ni naru: futari, tomodachi ni natta no? It's the same shape as line 6, where Mai says Yuki and Kenta gakkou de tomodachi ni natta (became friends at school). Mai answers from her own side in line 17 (tomodachi dekita yo: I've made a friend), but that's her reply, not Yuki's question. A is English 'make friends' turned into tsukuru: natives say tomodachi tsukuritai for wanting to go out and find friends, not for two people who've just hit it off. B is 'make' turned into ni suru, the 'make' partner of ni naru: tomodachi ni suru sounds like turning someone into your friend, not two people becoming friends.
edits.why: Explanation rewritten for the new choice B; it still points out the dekita/ni natta contrast heard in lines 16-17.

edits.value: shiken ka. jaa, kin'youbi wa? ...a, dame. hachiji made kaigi aru n datta.
edits.why: 金曜日 is きんようび. In kotoba romaji, n before y takes an apostrophe (kin'youbi, as in scripts 54 and 62). Without it, kinyoubi reads as きにょうび. The ja and kana are unchanged.

edits.value: a, dame. hachiji made kaigi ga iru n datta.
edits.why: Choice C (shigoto haitchatta) is something Yuki herself says in line 13, so a listener who remembers it could reasonably pick it. That breaks the heard rule. It is replaced with the classic aru/iru mix-up, which nobody says and is clearly wrong.

edits.value: Oh, that's no good. I need a meeting till eight.
edits.why: Gloss for the new choice C: after a thing, iru is heard as 要る (need).

edits.value: Line 5: a meeting on your calendar just exists, so it's kaigi ga aru (ga dropped, as usual in casual speech), and n datta adds 'oh right, I'd forgotten'. Kenji uses the same phrase in line 12 (mata kaigi aru no?). B puts English 'have' into Japanese with motsu: kaigi o motsu is at best a stiff 'hold a meeting', never a meeting you're going to. C swaps aru for iru, which is for people and animals; after a thing it's heard as iru 'need', so kaigi ga iru sounds like 'I need a meeting'. Meetings, classes and exams all take aru.
edits.why: Explanation rewritten for the new choice C.

edits.value: Line 9: jaa, ocha nomu? asoko ni mugicha aru yo. Yuki takes it in line 10 (un, ocha nomu). ocha is Japanese tea: green tea or, as here, barley tea (mugicha). B, koucha, is black tea, which is what English 'tea' usually means, but ocha on its own means Japanese tea, not black tea, and koucha isn't what's on offer. C, ocha shinai?, is an invitation to go out to a cafe for a break; Mai isn't suggesting going anywhere, she's offering the tea that's right there in the office.
edits.why: 'ocha never covers it' is too absolute: black tea is often counted as a kind of ocha (e.g. ocha no jikan). The real point is that ocha on its own means Japanese tea.

edits.value: dakara, kagi ga kaketeru tte!
edits.why: Without ga, casual 'kagi kaketeru tte!' means 'I've got it locked, I told you!', so it would be just as natural a reply here, and the gloss 'I'm locking it right now' is wrong. Use the brief's actual trap, kagi ga kaketeru: kakeru with ga, which is clearly wrong.

edits.value: I told you, it's locked! (kakeru, the act of locking, with ga)
edits.why: Gloss now matches the revised wrong choice (the ga + kakeru mistake for 'it's locked').

edits.value: Line 16: kagi kakatteru, the -teru form of kakaru: the lock is on. Sora found it that way in line 10 (kagi mo kakatteru yo), so he's describing how it is, not doing anything. A, kagi ga kaketeru, is the usual mistake for 'it's locked': kakeru is the act of locking, as in Mai's kagi kakete ne (lines 7 and 15), and with ga the verb is kakaru. B, rokku suru, is mostly for cars and phones, and it makes the door the thing you lock; at the front door it's the kagi that kakaru.
edits.why: The old explanation said kagi kaketeru could only mean 'locking it right now', which isn't true. Casual -teru on kakeru also means 'I've got it locked'. This rewrite explains the revised choice A.

edits.value: kodomo sodateru no, honto ni taihen na n da ne. oneesan, sugoi naa.
edits.why: The task asks the listener to say raising kids must be tough, but the old second model answer never says that. Its 毎日子供育ててる also sits oddly, since sodateru means raising a child over years.

edits.value: 子供育てるの、ほんとに大変なんだね。お姉さん、すごいなあ。
edits.why: Same change in Japanese, matching the new romaji.

edits.value: Raising kids really is tough, huh. Your sister's amazing.
edits.why: English for the new model answer.

edits.value: A cough 'comes out' like a fever does: seki ga deru, the same deru as Yuki's 'seki mo deru shi' in line 8 and her 'seki deteta yo ne?' to Kenta in line 10. English 'have a cough' pulls toward motsu, which isn't used; a cough that keeps coming takes deru (a clinic may also ask seki wa arimasu ka?). For coughing at this very moment, seki shiteru also works. Netsu wa nai is the negative of netsu ga aru.
edits.why: The old explanation called seki ga aru a trap. It is normal Japanese (clinics ask 咳はありますか？, and people say 熱はないけど咳がある), so only motsu is the real mistake.

edits.value: uwa, mabushii! kaaten shimatte!
edits.why: Sora really says kaaten akete in line 16, so wrong choice B repeated something he said, and the spoken question (ソラさんは何と言いましたか？) doesn't say which moment it means. This replaces it with the shimaru/shimeru mix-up, which nobody says in the script.

edits.value: Argh, that's bright! Curtains, shut! (shimaru, shutting on their own)
edits.why: Gloss for the new wrong choice B.

edits.value: Line 4: Kenta has just opened the curtains (line 3: kaaten akeru yo) and the light hurts (mabushii), so Sora wants them shut: kaaten shimete. A is English 'draw the curtains' put into Japanese word for word (hiku, pull). Japanese does have kaaten o hiku, but it's mostly written and, like 'draw', it doesn't say which way, so in speech people name the direction with shimeru or akeru. B uses shimaru, the curtains shutting on their own, like doa ga shimaru (kaaten shimatteru = the curtains are shut), so it can't ask someone to shut them; that takes shimeru. Kenta closes them with the same verb in lines 11 and 13 (kaaten shimeru ne, kaaten wa shimeta kedo), and Sora only asks for the opposite, kaaten akete, at the very end, once he's given up on sleep (line 16).
edits.why: Explanation rewritten for the new choice B. It also points out the kaaten akete Sora says in line 16.

edits.value: Well, no. I told my friend I'd miss the last train, and I was out of the bar by eleven.
edits.why: 'lose the last train' is not natural English. Line 3 of this script and the brief's own example both use 'miss'.

edits.value: That's right. If the train hadn't been late, I'd have missed the last train.
edits.why: Same fix as line 8. 'I'd have lost the last train' reads as a calque of nakunaru. The natural English is 'missed'.

edits.value: No, I'm not confident yet. I'm in your hands.
edits.why: yoroshiku onegai shimasu asks for his guidance and goodwill before the game, not for leniency. 'Please go easy on me' is a different set phrase (oteyawaraka ni onegai shimasu), so the gloss would teach the wrong meaning.

edits.value: sou. yoji ni ikkai, me ga sameta n da kedo, kimochi yokute okirenakatta.
edits.why: Without a comma, 一回目が覚めた reads as 一回目 (ikkaime, 'the first time') + ga sameta. Readers and TTS can take that path, which blurs the tested target me ga sameta. A comma after ikkai fixes the grouping. All three fields are changed together.

edits.value: そう。四時に一回、目が覚めたんだけど、気持ちよくて起きれなかった。
edits.why: Comma after 一回 so it can't be read as the ordinal 一回目 ('the first time') and the voice groups 目が覚めた as one chunk.

edits.value: そう。よじにいっかい、めがさめたんだけど、きもちよくておきれなかった。
edits.why: Same comma in the kana. Without it, いっかいめがさめた has the same ikkaime ambiguity.

edits.value: Sora says, "yoji ni ikkai, me ga sameta n da kedo, kimochi yokute okirenakatta." What happened at four o'clock?
edits.why: Keeps the quoted line in step with the edited romaji of line 6.

edits.value: 'I saw a bad dream' (miru, word for word)
edits.why: Only the two wrong glosses were marked '(..., word for word)' and the right one was a plain 'I had a bad dream.', so the answer showed without listening. Giving C the same literal gloss style means the learner has to remember the verb they heard (mita).

edits.value: de, kesa satou-san ni mo guchi ittara ne, kenji, keeki no omise de baito shiteru n da tte!
edits.why: Romaji convention: copula and the quotative tte are separate words. Every other draft spells the hearsay ending n da tte; this was the only n datte.

edits.value: honto ni? yokatta. jaa, ashita wa gakkou ikeru ne.
edits.why: Said flat, 'gakkou iku ne' sounds like Yuki saying she'll go to school herself, and learners are taught to hear 'iku ne' that way. A sister would say 'ikeru ne' here (so you can go), which clearly means Kenji and still uses gakkou ni iku.

edits.value: ほんとに？よかった。じゃあ、明日は学校行けるね。
edits.why: Keeps ja in step with the romaji fix: 行けるね points the line at Kenji.

edits.value: ほんとに？よかった。じゃあ、あしたはがっこういけるね。
edits.why: Keeps kana in step with the romaji and ja fix.

edits.value: Really? Great. So you can go to school tomorrow, then.
edits.why: English now matches ikeru (can go). Kenji's reply 'a, un. iku yo.' still follows.

edits.value: Kenta uses it in line 1 (yuki to nomi ni itta koto, nakatta yo ne) and line 15 (issho ni nomi ni ikeru ne), and Yuki uses it in line 14 (shigoto no hito to nomi ni iku to). On its own, nomi already means drinking alcohol, so you don't need osake. It's the drinking version of gohan ni iku, which Yuki uses for going out to eat (lines 2 and 18). Friends also invite with plain nomou (kondo nomou yo, let's grab a drink sometime), but nomi ni iku is the clearest way to suggest going out for one.
edits.why: The explanation claimed plain nomou is only said with a glass in front of you. That's false: kondo nomou yo and kyou nomanai? are everyday invitations to go out drinking.

edits.value: The important thing Sora's mom calls about is just whether he's eating. Sora hangs up on her, and when she calls Kenta, Kenta tells her Sora is right there.
edits.why: The right answer said she 'only wants to know if he's eating', but in line 12 she wants to go on about yesterday (ato ne, kinou no koto na n da kedo). A careful listener could reject the right choice on that detail.

edits.value: meeru okuru n ja nai?
edits.why: Choice A ('meeru okutta n ja nai?') is something Kenji actually says, word for word, in line 10 ('sore, chigau bangou ni meeru okutta n ja nai?'). A heard question's wrong choice must not be something a character said. This version keeps the okuru/kuru direction contrast in a form nobody says, and it clearly doesn't fit a phone that has just gone off.

edits.value: Aren't you going to send an email?
edits.why: Gloss for the new choice A romaji (meeru okuru n ja nai?).

edits.value: Line 8: a, sumaho natta yo. meeru kita n ja nai? In Japanese the email is the one that comes: meeru (ga) kita, 'an email came', and Mom answers honto da, meeru kita! A, okuru, is the other direction, sending, which makes no sense when her phone has just gone off; Kenji uses okuru only for her email going out to the wrong number (line 10). C, uketoru, is English 'receive' word for word, but it sounds stiff and is for parcels and documents, not emails.
edits.why: The old explanation defended choice A as something Kenji says in line 10. A now asks whether she's about to send an email, so the explanation has to say why that's wrong.

edits.value: ユキさんは、病院までどう行くと言いましたか？
edits.why: 病院までの道を何と言いましたか reads as 'what did she call the road'; どう行くと言いましたか is the natural way to ask how she said to get there.

edits.value: ゆきさんは、びょういんまでどういくといいましたか？
edits.why: Keeps the kana in step with the corrected ja.

edits.value: yuki-san wa, byouin made dou iku to iimashita ka?
edits.why: Keeps the romaji in step with the corrected ja.

edits.value: Seven in the morning. Satou-san, the elderly man next door, leaves a voicemail for Kenta, who told him yesterday that he never eats breakfast. Yesterday Satou-san also baked his first ever loaf of bread, and it came out far too big for one person.
edits.why: The setting said he 'has just baked' the bread, but line 3 (kinou hajimete pan o yaite mita) and question 4 both put the baking yesterday.

edits.value: Sugar going into a drink is ireru in its plain 'put in' sense: Satou-san says koohii ni osatou o mittsu mo iremasu yo ne (line 7) and ocha ni wa osatou, irenaide kudasai ne (line 9). English 'I take sugar' has no match: satou o toru means picking the sugar up (satou totte = pass me the sugar), not having it in your coffee. Mai's koohii ireta is the other ireru, brewing the cup. With a friend plain satou is fine; Satou-san says osatou because he's speaking politely. (satou, sugar, has the same sounds as his name, only the pitch differs; the o- is politeness, but it also keeps the two apart.) If you do want it black: burakku de ii yo.
edits.why: 砂糖 (sa-TO-u) and 佐藤 (SA-tou) differ in pitch accent, so 'sounds exactly like his name' is wrong for a learner who only hears the audio.

edits.value: Mai is worried she's failed, but when the results come out at twelve, she has passed on her first try.
edits.why: The correct gist choice overstates the audio. Mai only says she might not have got seventy (nanajutten mo toretenai kamo shiremasen) and worries what she'll do if she failed (ochitara dou shiyou). She is never sure, and the explanation itself says she 'fears' it.

edits.value: Tanaka-san says it this way in line 13 (ikkai de shiken ni ukatta) and line 9 (yatto ukatta). ukaru and ukeru are one sound apart, and line 9 has both: shiken o sankai ukete, yatto ukatta (took it three times, finally passed). shiken o ukarimashita is wrong: the exam takes ni. Tanaka-san asks politely, so answer with -masu.
edits.why: The explanation says 'ukarimashita and ukemashita are one sound apart', but u-ka-ri-ma-shi-ta and u-ke-ma-shi-ta differ by more than one sound (kari vs ke). Only the dictionary forms ukaru and ukeru are one sound apart, so the claim is corrected to those.

77.title: Persimmons from next door
77.setting: Saturday morning outside a small apartment building. Yuki has come down to the mailboxes in her sweatpants, her washing still sitting in the machine upstairs. Next door, Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, is hanging out his laundry beside a basket of persimmons he has just picked from his tree.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu, yuki-san. kyou wa sentakumono ga yoku kawakisou desu ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます、ユキさん。今日は洗濯物がよく乾きそうですね。
lines.kana: おはようございます、ゆきさん。きょうはせんたくものがよくかわきそうですね。
lines.english: Good morning, Yuki. Looks like a good day for drying laundry.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. sou desu ne. demo kyou wa nanka, yaruki ga nai n desu yo ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます。そうですね。でも今日はなんか、やる気がないんですよね。
lines.kana: おはようございます。そうですね。でもきょうはなんか、やるきがないんですよね。
lines.english: Good morning. It does. But today I just can't be bothered.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dou shita n desu ka? shigoto ga isogashikatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: どうしたんですか？仕事が忙しかったんですか？
lines.kana: どうしたんですか？しごとがいそがしかったんですか？
lines.english: What's the matter? Has work been busy?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. konshuu wa zutto isogashikute, sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu.
lines.ja: はい。今週はずっと忙しくて、ストレスが溜まってるんです。
lines.kana: はい。こんしゅうはずっといそがしくて、すとれすがたまってるんです。
lines.english: Yes. It's been non-stop all week, and the stress has really piled up.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa taihen deshita ne. sutoresu ga tamaru to, yaruki mo naku narimasu yo ne.
lines.ja: それは大変でしたね。ストレスが溜まると、やる気もなくなりますよね。
lines.kana: それはたいへんでしたね。すとれすがたまると、やるきもなくなりますよね。
lines.english: That must have been hard. When stress piles up, your motivation goes too, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou wa kaji o shiyou to omotteta n desu kedo, zenzen yaruki ga denakute.
lines.ja: 今日は家事をしようと思ってたんですけど、全然やる気が出なくて。
lines.kana: きょうはかじをしようとおもってたんですけど、ぜんぜんやるきがでなくて。
lines.english: I meant to do the housework today, but I just can't get myself going.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yaruki wa ne, hajimetara dete kuru mono desu yo. mazu wa chotto dake, yatte mitara dou desu ka?
lines.ja: やる気はね、始めたら出てくるものですよ。まずはちょっとだけ、やってみたらどうですか？
lines.kana: やるきはね、はじめたらでてくるものですよ。まずはちょっとだけ、やってみたらどうですか？
lines.english: Motivation, you know, comes once you've started. Why not try doing just a little first?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hajimetara, desu ka. demo, sono hajimeru yaruki ga nai n desu yo.
lines.ja: 始めたら、ですか。でも、その始めるやる気がないんですよ。
lines.kana: はじめたら、ですか。でも、そのはじめるやるきがないんですよ。
lines.english: Once I've started, huh? But I don't even have the motivation to start.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, uchi no kaki, douzo. tabete, genki dashite kudasai.
lines.ja: じゃあ、うちの柿、どうぞ。食べて、元気出してください。
lines.kana: じゃあ、うちのかき、どうぞ。たべて、げんきだしてください。
lines.english: Well then, have some persimmons from my tree. Eat them and cheer up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, kaki! daisuki na n desu. uwaa, tenshon agarimasu!
lines.ja: え、柿！大好きなんです。うわあ、テンション上がります！
lines.kana: え、かき！だいすきなんです。うわあ、てんしょんあがります！
lines.english: Oh, persimmons! I love them. Wow, I'm getting all excited!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tenshon ga agaru, desu ka. omoshiroi iikata desu ne.
lines.ja: テンションが上がる、ですか。面白い言い方ですね。
lines.kana: てんしょんがあがる、ですか。おもしろいいいかたですね。
lines.english: "Tenshon ga agaru," is it? What a fun way to put it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. nanka mou, genki ga demashita.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。なんかもう、元気が出ました。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。なんかもう、げんきがでました。
lines.english: Thank you. I feel better already.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa yokatta. sutoresu ga tamatta toki wa, oishii mono ga ichiban desu yo.
lines.ja: それはよかった。ストレスが溜まった時は、おいしいものが一番ですよ。
lines.kana: それはよかった。すとれすがたまったときは、おいしいものがいちばんですよ。
lines.english: I'm glad. When stress builds up, something tasty is the best cure.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, yaruki mo chotto dete kimashita. mazu sentakumono, hoshite kimasu!
lines.ja: あ、やる気もちょっと出てきました。まず洗濯物、干してきます！
lines.kana: あ、やるきもちょっとでてきました。まずせんたくもの、ほしてきます！
lines.english: Oh, I'm even getting a bit motivated. I'll go and hang out my laundry first!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. yuki-san ga genki da to, watashi mo genki ga demasu yo.
lines.ja: いいですね。ユキさんが元気だと、私も元気が出ますよ。
lines.kana: いいですね。ゆきさんがげんきだと、わたしもげんきがでますよ。
lines.english: Good for you. When you're cheerful, it gives me a lift too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, jaa satou-san mo, tenshon agarimashita?
lines.ja: え、じゃあ佐藤さんも、テンション上がりました？
lines.kana: え、じゃあさとうさんも、てんしょんあがりました？
lines.english: Oh, so you're all hyped up too, Satou-san?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ee, tenshon agarimashita yo. hajimete tsukaimashita.
lines.ja: ええ、テンション上がりましたよ。初めて使いました。
lines.kana: ええ、てんしょんあがりましたよ。はじめてつかいました。
lines.english: Yes, very hyped. That's the first time I've ever said it.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Satou-san offers to hang out Yuki's laundry for her, since she's worn out from work.
Yuki decides to skip the housework and rest today, as Satou-san suggests.
Yuki can't face the housework, but Satou-san's persimmons cheer her up and she goes off to hang out her laundry.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-8: after a stressful week, Yuki has no motivation (yaruki ga nai) and can't get going on the housework (yaruki ga denakute). In line 9 Satou-san gives her persimmons from his tree; she gets excited (line 10), feels better (line 12), and in line 14 goes off to hang out her laundry. A is wrong: Satou-san never offers to do her laundry; he tells her to try doing a little herself (line 7). B is wrong: he says motivation comes once you start, not that she should rest, and she doesn't take the day off: she starts with the laundry (line 14).

questions.english: It's Sunday and you just want to lie around. Kenta asks you, "nee, kyou nani suru? dokka ikanai?" Tell him you just don't feel like it today, using yaruki ga nai.
questions.ja: ねえ、今日何する？どっか行かない？
questions.kana: ねえ、きょうなにする？どっかいかない？
questions.romaji: nee, kyou nani suru? dokka ikanai?
questions.answer: Say you can't be bothered today: kyou wa nanka yaruki nai. With a friend ga can drop, and gomen softens it.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa nanka yaruki nai. uchi ni iru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日はなんかやる気ない。うちにいるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I just can't be bothered today. I'm staying in.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa yaruki ga nai n da. mata kondo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はやる気がないんだ。また今度ね。
modelAnswers.english: I've got no motivation today. Another time, OK?

questions.explanation: In line 2 Yuki tells Satou-san kyou wa nanka, yaruki ga nai n desu yo ne (today I just can't be bothered), and in line 8 she says she doesn't even have the motivation to start (sono hajimeru yaruki ga nai n desu yo). About yourself, yaruki nai is a flat 'I don't feel like it'; about someone else (ano hito yaruki nai) it's a criticism. Avoid yaruki ga arimasen: it sounds stiff, and even politely people say yaruki ga nai n desu, as Yuki does. Kenta is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: Satou-san tells Yuki how motivation works. When does he say it comes?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、やる気はいつ出ると言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、やるきはいつでるといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, yaruki wa itsu deru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: After a proper rest, so she should take the morning off first.
Once she gets started, so she should try doing just a little first.
When she eats something tasty, like his persimmons.

questions.explanation: In line 7 Satou-san says yaruki wa ne, hajimetara dete kuru mono desu yo: motivation comes out (deru) once you start, so try a little first. Yuki uses the negative in line 6 (zenzen yaruki ga denakute, I just can't get going), and in line 14 it finally comes: yaruki mo chotto dete kimashita. A is wrong: he never tells her to rest; his advice is to start. C mixes up yaruki with genki: the persimmons are to lift her mood (genki dashite, line 9), and good food is his cure for stress (line 13), not where motivation comes from.

questions.english: You've had an awful day at work. Mai hands you a hot coffee and says, "hai, kore. muri shinaide ne." Thank her and tell her it's cheered you up, using genki ga deru.
questions.ja: はい、これ。無理しないでね。
questions.kana: はい、これ。むりしないでね。
questions.romaji: hai, kore. muri shinaide ne.
questions.answer: Thank her and say it gave you a lift, in the past: arigatou, genki deta. It's about you, so it's deta; genki dashite is what you say to cheer someone else up.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. nanka genki deta.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。なんか元気出た。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. That's cheered me up.

modelAnswers.romaji: uwaa, ureshii. arigatou, sugoku genki deta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うわあ、うれしい。ありがとう、すごく元気出たよ。
modelAnswers.english: Aw, that's so nice. Thanks, it's really cheered me up.

questions.explanation: In line 9 Satou-san hands Yuki persimmons and says tabete, genki dashite kudasai (eat them and cheer up): genki dashite is what you say to someone else. In line 12 Yuki answers about herself: nanka mou, genki ga demashita (I feel better already), and in line 15 Satou-san says her cheerfulness gives him a lift too (watashi mo genki ga demasu yo). For 'that cheered me up', use the past genki deta. Don't answer genki dashite, which would tell Mai to cheer up, and genki ni natta usually means you've got over an illness. Mai is a friend, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Yuki sees the persimmons, what does she say?
questions.ja: 柿を見て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: かきをみて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kaki o mite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I'm getting so excited!
choices.romaji: tenshon agarimasu!

choices.english: I'm getting all worked up!
choices.romaji: koufun shimasu!

choices.english: What a downer!
choices.romaji: tenshon sagarimasu!

questions.explanation: In line 10 Yuki sees the persimmons and says uwaa, tenshon agarimasu! (wow, I'm getting all excited!). Satou-san repeats it in line 11 as a fun, young-sounding expression and tries it himself in lines 16-17. B is the English speaker's trap: koufun shimasu sounds agitated or even sexual, not happily excited. C is the opposite, tenshon sagaru (get bummed out), which doesn't fit someone who loves persimmons. And tenshon is mood or hype, not 'tension' (that's kinchou).

questions.english: You've been working late every night. Your manager, Tanaka-san, asks you, "saikin, tsukaretemasen ka? daijoubu desu ka?" Tell him honestly that stress has been piling up, using sutoresu ga tamaru.
questions.ja: 最近、疲れてませんか？大丈夫ですか？
questions.kana: さいきん、つかれてませんか？だいじょうぶですか？
questions.romaji: saikin, tsukaretemasen ka? daijoubu desu ka?
questions.answer: Tell him stress has built up, politely since he's your manager: sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu. Stress piles up (tamaru); it isn't a verb you do.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, saikin chotto sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、最近ちょっとストレスが溜まってるんです。
modelAnswers.english: To be honest, the stress has been piling up a bit lately.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. demo, chotto sutoresu ga tamatte kimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。でも、ちょっとストレスが溜まってきました。
modelAnswers.english: I'm OK. But the stress is starting to build up a bit.

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki tells Satou-san that after a busy week, sutoresu ga tamatteru n desu (the stress has piled up); he picks it up in line 5 (sutoresu ga tamaru to, when stress piles up) and again in line 13. Use tamatteru for how you are now. Don't say sutoresu shiteru: stress isn't something you do in Japanese, it's something that piles up. Hear the contrast in the scene: stress piles up (tamaru), while Yuki's mood goes up (tenshon agaru, line 10). Tanaka-san is your manager, so answer politely.

78.title: Yesterday's bento
78.setting: Sunday lunchtime at Kenta and Sora's flat. Last night Kenta made hot pot for Yuki and Mai. Mai drops by to pick up the glasses she left behind, just as Sora, barely awake, is about to heat up a bento he bought yesterday.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora, kinou nando mo renraku shita n da yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、昨日何度も連絡したんだよ。
lines.kana: そら、きのうなんどもれんらくしたんだよ。
lines.english: Sora, I messaged you loads of times last night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, juuden kireteta. dou shita no?
lines.ja: ごめん、充電切れてた。どうしたの？
lines.kana: ごめん、じゅうでんきれてた。どうしたの？
lines.english: Sorry, my battery was dead. What's up?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: megane, koko ni nai? kinou, nabe no toki hazushite, wasurechatta.
lines.ja: メガネ、ここにない？昨日、鍋のとき外して、忘れちゃった。
lines.kana: めがね、ここにない？きのう、なべのときはずして、わすれちゃった。
lines.english: Are my glasses here? I took them off while we were having hot pot and left them behind.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, are mai no ka. hora, kore.
lines.ja: ああ、あれマイのか。ほら、これ。
lines.kana: ああ、あれまいのか。ほら、これ。
lines.english: Oh, so those were yours. Here you go.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: yokatta, arigatou. are, ima kara ohiru?
lines.ja: よかった、ありがとう。あれ、今からお昼？
lines.kana: よかった、ありがとう。あれ、いまからおひる？
lines.english: Phew, thanks. Oh, are you just having lunch?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. kinou katta obentou, renji de atatameru tokoro.
lines.ja: うん。昨日買ったお弁当、レンジで温めるところ。
lines.kana: うん。きのうかったおべんとう、れんじであたためるところ。
lines.english: Yeah. I'm about to microwave the bento I bought yesterday.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kinou? sore, reizouko ni ireta?
lines.ja: 昨日？それ、冷蔵庫に入れた？
lines.kana: きのう？それ、れいぞうこにいれた？
lines.english: Yesterday? Did you put it in the fridge?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uun, zutto koko ni atta. nabe tabete, wasureteta.
lines.ja: ううん、ずっとここにあった。鍋食べて、忘れてた。
lines.kana: ううん、ずっとここにあった。なべたべて、わすれてた。
lines.english: Nope, it's been sitting here the whole time. We had hot pot and I forgot all about it.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, kore, kigen kireteru yo. kinou no yoru juuji made.
lines.ja: あ、これ、期限切れてるよ。昨日の夜十時まで。
lines.kana: あ、これ、きげんきれてるよ。きのうのよるじゅうじまで。
lines.english: Oh, this is past its date. It was only good till ten last night.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: demo, kigen chotto kireta dake desho? obentou wa atatamereba daijoubu da yo.
lines.ja: でも、期限ちょっと切れただけでしょ？お弁当は温めれば大丈夫だよ。
lines.kana: でも、きげんちょっときれただけでしょ？おべんとうはあたためればだいじょうぶだよ。
lines.english: But it's only just past, right? A bento's fine if you heat it up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: dame da yo. reizouko ni iretenakatta shi, kigen mo kireteru n da kara.
lines.ja: だめだよ。冷蔵庫に入れてなかったし、期限も切れてるんだから。
lines.kana: だめだよ。れいぞうこにいれてなかったし、きげんもきれてるんだから。
lines.english: No way. It wasn't in the fridge, and it's past its date as well.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: aa, obentou atatamete taberu tsumori datta noni.
lines.ja: ああ、お弁当温めて食べるつもりだったのに。
lines.kana: ああ、おべんとうあたためてたべるつもりだったのに。
lines.english: Aw, and I was going to heat it up and have it for lunch.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kinou no nabe, mada aru n ja nai?
lines.ja: 昨日の鍋、まだあるんじゃない？
lines.kana: きのうのなべ、まだあるんじゃない？
lines.english: Isn't there still some hot pot left from last night?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, sou da. kenta ga futa shite, reizouko ni iretoite kureta n da.
lines.ja: あ、そうだ。ケンタが蓋して、冷蔵庫に入れといてくれたんだ。
lines.kana: あ、そうだ。けんたがふたして、れいぞうこにいれといてくれたんだ。
lines.english: Oh, right. Kenta put the lid on and stuck it in the fridge for us.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto da, mada ippai aru. sasuga kenta.
lines.ja: ほんとだ、まだいっぱいある。さすがケンタ。
lines.kana: ほんとだ、まだいっぱいある。さすがけんた。
lines.english: So there is, and loads of it. Good old Kenta.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, futa shite, gofun gurai atatameyou.
lines.ja: じゃあ、蓋して、五分ぐらい温めよう。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ふたして、ごふんぐらいあたためよう。
lines.english: Right, lid on, and we'll heat it for about five minutes.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. kondo kara, obentou wa sugu reizouko ni iretoite ne.
lines.ja: うん。今度から、お弁当はすぐ冷蔵庫に入れといてね。
lines.kana: うん。こんどから、おべんとうはすぐれいぞうこにいれといてね。
lines.english: OK. And from now on, put your bento straight in the fridge, alright?

questions.english: What happened with Sora's lunch?
questions.ja: ソラのお昼は、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: そらのおひるは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora no ohiru wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: The microwave wasn't working, so they heated his bento up in a pot instead.
His bento had been left out all night and was past its date, so they heated up the leftover hot pot instead.
Kenta had already finished the leftover hot pot, so Sora heated up his bento after all.

questions.explanation: Sora bought the bento yesterday and it sat out all night (lines 6-8). Mai finds its date ran out at ten last night (line 9) and won't let him eat it, even heated (lines 10-11). So they heat up the hot pot Kenta put in the fridge (lines 13-16). A is wrong: the microwave is never a problem, the bento itself is. C is wrong: the hot pot is still there, and plenty of it (line 15).

questions.english: Sora came over for hot pot at your place, and there's a lot left. He asks, "nabe, mada ippai aru ne. dou suru?" Say you'll put it in the fridge, using reizouko ni ireru.
questions.ja: 鍋、まだいっぱいあるね。どうする？
questions.kana: なべ、まだいっぱいあるね。どうする？
questions.romaji: nabe, mada ippai aru ne. dou suru?
questions.answer: Say it goes in the fridge: reizouko ni ireru, with ni for where the food goes. With -toku it means putting it in there for later: reizouko ni iretoku ne (I'll put it in the fridge).

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, reizouko ni iretoku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、冷蔵庫に入れとくね。
modelAnswers.english: I'll put it in the fridge, then.

modelAnswers.romaji: futa shite, reizouko ni irete okou. ashita mo taberareru shi.
modelAnswers.ja: 蓋して、冷蔵庫に入れておこう。明日も食べられるし。
modelAnswers.english: Let's put the lid on and put it in the fridge. We can have it tomorrow too.

questions.explanation: Mai asks 'reizouko ni ireta?' (did you put it in the fridge?) in line 7, Sora says Kenta 'reizouko ni iretoite kureta' (put it in the fridge for us) in line 14, and Mai ends with 'reizouko ni iretoite ne' in line 17. The verb is ireru, put inside; oku, the English 'put', is setting something down on a surface. Keep ni: it marks where the food goes, unlike satou o ireru, where o marks what goes in.

questions.english: Mai tells Sora his bento is past its date. What does Sora say about it?
questions.ja: ソラは、お弁当について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらは、おべんとうについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa, obentou ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It would be fine if he put it in the fridge for a while first.
It tastes fine cold, so there's no need to heat it.
It would be fine to eat as long as he heated it up.

questions.explanation: Line 10: 'obentou wa atatamereba daijoubu da yo' (a bento's fine if you heat it up). atatameru is heating food up, and -ba makes it 'if you heat it'. A is wrong: he says nothing about the fridge, and the bento had never been in it, which is Mai's point in line 11. B is wrong: he wants it hot. In line 6 he was about to heat it in the microwave ('renji de atatameru tokoro'), and in line 12 he says he'd planned to heat it up and eat it.

questions.english: There's still plenty of hot pot left. What does Sora say as they heat it up?
questions.ja: 鍋を温めるとき、ソラは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: なべをあたためるとき、そらはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: nabe o atatameru toki, sora wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: lid on, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa shite, gofun gurai atatameyou.

choices.english: set the lid down, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa oite, gofun gurai atatameyou.

choices.english: lid off, and heat it for about five minutes
choices.romaji: jaa, futa totte, gofun gurai atatameyou.

questions.explanation: Line 16: 'futa shite' (put the lid on). A lid goes on with suru, the same suru as masuku o suru, and Kenta did the same before the pot went in the fridge (line 14: 'futa shite, reizouko ni iretoite kureta'). B is the English 'put the lid on' turned word for word into futa o oku, which means setting the lid down somewhere, so the pot would heat uncovered. C, futa o toru, takes the lid off: the opposite of what Sora does after Mai has looked inside.

questions.english: Sora offers you a bento from yesterday. You check the label: its date ran out last night. He asks, "kore, kinou no obentou da kedo, taberu?" Tell him it's past its date, using kigen ga kireru.
questions.ja: これ、昨日のお弁当だけど、食べる？
questions.kana: これ、きのうのおべんとうだけど、たべる？
questions.romaji: kore, kinou no obentou da kedo, taberu?
questions.answer: Say it's past its date: kigen kireteru (ga often drops in casual talk), with kireru, the verb for something running out. Then turn it down.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, sore kigen kireteru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、それ期限切れてるよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, that's past its date.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kigen ga kireteru kara, yametoku.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、期限が切れてるから、やめとく。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, it's past its date, so I'll pass.

questions.explanation: Mai says 'kigen kireteru yo' in line 9 and 'kigen mo kireteru' in line 11, and Sora's 'kigen chotto kireta dake desho?' in line 10 is the past form. 'Expire' needs no special verb: a date runs out with kireru, just as Sora's phone battery did in line 2 ('juuden kireteta'). Don't mix it up with kigen ga warui, 'in a bad mood', which is a different kigen.

80.title: Rained Off
80.setting: A Sunday evening. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, leaves a voicemail for Kenta, who lent him a tent for a camping trip with some old friends. Rain spoiled part of their plan, and Satou-san has an idea for next Saturday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, kenta-kun? satou desu. tento, kashite kurete arigatou gozaimashita.
lines.ja: もしもし、ケンタくん？佐藤です。テント、貸してくれてありがとうございました。
lines.kana: もしもし、けんたくん？さとうです。てんと、かしてくれてありがとうございました。
lines.english: Hello, Kenta? It's Satou. Thank you for lending me your tent.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kinou kara, mukashi no tomodachi to kyanpu ni itteta n desu. sakki kaette kimashita.
lines.ja: 昨日から、昔の友達とキャンプに行ってたんです。さっき帰ってきました。
lines.kana: きのうから、むかしのともだちときゃんぷにいってたんです。さっきかえってきました。
lines.english: I've been away camping with some old friends since yesterday. I just got back.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hontou wa, kinou minna de yama ni noboru tsumori datta n desu kedo, ame de dame deshita.
lines.ja: 本当は、昨日みんなで山に登るつもりだったんですけど、雨でだめでした。
lines.kana: ほんとうは、きのうみんなでやまにのぼるつもりだったんですけど、あめでだめでした。
lines.english: We'd actually planned to climb a mountain together yesterday, but the rain put a stop to that.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sorede, kawari ni tsuri ni itta n desu. maa, nanimo tsuremasen deshita kedo ne.
lines.ja: それで、代わりに釣りに行ったんです。まあ、何も釣れませんでしたけどね。
lines.kana: それで、かわりにつりにいったんです。まあ、なにもつれませんでしたけどね。
lines.english: So we went fishing instead. Not that we caught a thing.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: demo, minna de zutto hanashitete, ii kibun tenkan ni narimashita yo.
lines.ja: でも、みんなでずっと話してて、いい気分転換になりましたよ。
lines.kana: でも、みんなでずっとはなしてて、いいきぶんてんかんになりましたよ。
lines.english: But we chatted the whole time, and it made a really nice change of pace.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou ieba kenta-kun, mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai tte, ittemashita yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえばケンタくん、もう三年もキャンプに行ってないって、言ってましたよね。
lines.kana: そういえばけんたくん、もうさんねんもきゃんぷにいってないって、いってましたよね。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Kenta, you told me you hadn't been camping in three whole years.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: saikin wa shigoto bakkari de, zenzen karada o ugokashitenai tte.
lines.ja: 最近は仕事ばっかりで、全然体を動かしてないって。
lines.kana: さいきんはしごとばっかりで、ぜんぜんからだをうごかしてないって。
lines.english: And that lately it's been all work, and you haven't been moving your body at all.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: raishuu no doyoubi, minna de mou ichido, ano yama ni noboru n desu. kenta-kun mo issho ni dou desu ka?
lines.ja: 来週の土曜日、みんなでもう一度、あの山に登るんです。ケンタくんも一緒にどうですか？
lines.kana: らいしゅうのどようび、みんなでもういちど、あのやまにのぼるんです。けんたくんもいっしょにどうですか？
lines.english: Next Saturday we're all having another go at that mountain. Why don't you come along?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: chiisai yama desu kara, toshi o totta watashi demo noboremasu. demo, chanto karada o ugokasemasu yo.
lines.ja: 小さい山ですから、年をとった私でも登れます。でも、ちゃんと体を動かせますよ。
lines.kana: ちいさいやまですから、としをとったわたしでものぼれます。でも、ちゃんとからだをうごかせますよ。
lines.english: It's a small one, so even an old man like me can climb it. But you'll still get some proper exercise.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: shigoto de sutoresu mo tamatteru deshou? tama ni wa kibun tenkan shinai to.
lines.ja: 仕事でストレスもたまってるでしょう？たまには気分転換しないと。
lines.kana: しごとですとれすもたまってるでしょう？たまにはきぶんてんかんしないと。
lines.english: Work must be getting you stressed, too. You need a change of pace now and then.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yama ni nobotte kara, mata tsuri ni iku tsumori desu. sore mo ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
lines.ja: 山に登ってから、また釣りに行くつもりです。それもいい気分転換になりますよ。
lines.kana: やまにのぼってから、またつりにいくつもりです。それもいいきぶんてんかんになりますよ。
lines.english: After the climb, we're planning to go fishing again. That'll do you good, too.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, doyoubi wa asa yoji ni demasu kara ne. jaa, renraku mattemasu.
lines.ja: あ、土曜日は朝四時に出ますからね。じゃあ、連絡待ってます。
lines.kana: あ、どようびはあさよじにでますからね。じゃあ、れんらくまってます。
lines.english: Oh, and on Saturday we leave at four in the morning. Well, let me know.

questions.english: Why does Satou-san call Kenta?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、どうしてケンタくんに電話しましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、どうしてけんたくんにでんわしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, doushite kenta-kun ni denwa shimashita ka?

choices.english: To say the rain spoiled the whole trip, so he's bringing the tent back and staying home next weekend.
To thank him for the tent and invite him to climb the mountain with them next Saturday, after rain stopped them this time.
To tell him they caught lots of fish, and ask him to come fishing with them early tomorrow morning.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Satou-san thanks Kenta for lending him the tent. Lines 3-4: rain stopped them climbing the mountain, so they went fishing instead. Line 8: they're all having another go at that mountain next Saturday, and he asks Kenta to come, since Kenta said he hadn't been getting any exercise (line 7). A is wrong: the rain only stopped the climb, the trip was still a nice change of pace (line 5), and he's going out again next Saturday and wants Kenta along. C is wrong: they didn't catch a thing (line 4), and the outing is next Saturday, leaving at four in the morning (line 12), not tomorrow.

questions.english: Your friend Sora has spent all Sunday indoors. In the evening he stretches and groans, "kyou mo zutto uchi de geemu shiteta. nanka karada ga darui naa." Tell him he needs to get some exercise now and then, using karada o ugokasu.
questions.ja: 今日もずっとうちでゲームしてた。なんか体がだるいなあ。
questions.kana: きょうもずっとうちでげーむしてた。なんかからだがだるいなあ。
questions.romaji: kyou mo zutto uchi de geemu shiteta. nanka karada ga darui naa.
questions.answer: Tell him to get moving: tama ni wa karada (o) ugokasanakya (you've got to get some exercise now and then), or suggest doing it together with karada o ugokasou. It's ugokasu, with o.

modelAnswers.romaji: zutto uchi ni iru kara da yo. tama ni wa karada ugokasanakya.
modelAnswers.ja: ずっとうちにいるからだよ。たまには体動かさなきゃ。
modelAnswers.english: That's because you've been stuck indoors all day. You've got to get some exercise now and then.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita, issho ni soto de karada o ugokasou yo. sukoshi demo zenzen chigau kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日、一緒に外で体を動かそうよ。少しでも全然違うから。
modelAnswers.english: Let's go out and get some exercise together tomorrow. Even a little makes a big difference.

questions.explanation: Satou-san reminds Kenta he said he hadn't been moving his body at all (zenzen karada o ugokashitenai, line 7), and promises the small mountain still gives a proper workout (chanto karada o ugokasemasu, line 9). karada o ugokasu is the everyday way to talk about getting exercise, anything from a walk to a climb, and casual speech often drops the o (karada ugokasanakya). ugokasu means move something, so it takes o; ugoku is move by itself, so karada o ugoku is wrong, and karada ga ugokanai means you physically can't move. undou suru (exercise) works too, but it leans towards sport and the gym.

questions.english: Your manager Tanaka-san looks worn out on Friday afternoon and says, "saikin isogashikute, shuumatsu mo shigoto no koto bakari kangaete shimau n desu yo." Suggest something for the weekend and tell him it'll do him good, using kibun tenkan ni naru.
questions.ja: 最近忙しくて、週末も仕事のことばかり考えてしまうんですよ。
questions.kana: さいきんいそがしくて、しゅうまつもしごとのことばかりかんがえてしまうんですよ。
questions.romaji: saikin isogashikute, shuumatsu mo shigoto no koto bakari kangaete shimau n desu yo.
questions.answer: Suggest an outing (tsuri ni itte mitara dou desu ka?) and add ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo (it'd be a nice change of pace). Keep it polite with Tanaka-san: narimasu, not naru.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, shuumatsu wa tsuri ni itte mitara dou desu ka? ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、週末は釣りに行ってみたらどうですか？いい気分転換になりますよ。
modelAnswers.english: Then why not try going fishing this weekend? It'd be a nice change of pace.

modelAnswers.romaji: tama ni wa yama ni nobotte mitara dou desu ka? kitto ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: たまには山に登ってみたらどうですか？きっといい気分転換になりますよ。
modelAnswers.english: How about climbing a mountain for once? I'm sure it'd do you good.

questions.explanation: Satou-san says the rained-off trip still made ii kibun tenkan ni narimashita (a nice change of pace, line 5), and that fishing after the climb will be ii kibun tenkan ni narimasu too (line 11). kibun tenkan ni naru, usually with ii, says something does you good as a break, which makes it the natural phrase for encouraging someone. kibun tenkan suru is taking the break yourself: in line 10 Satou-san tells Kenta tama ni wa kibun tenkan shinai to (you need to take a break now and then). kibarashi ni naru works the same way, but leans towards taking your mind off something bad.

questions.english: On Monday your friend Yuki says, "shuumatsu, nani shiteta no? zutto renraku nakatta kedo." You didn't answer because you were climbing a mountain with friends on Saturday. Tell her, using yama ni noboru.
questions.ja: 週末、何してたの？ずっと連絡なかったけど。
questions.kana: しゅうまつ、なにしてたの？ずっとれんらくなかったけど。
questions.romaji: shuumatsu, nani shiteta no? zutto renraku nakatta kedo.
questions.answer: Say you were up a mountain with friends: tomodachi to yama ni nobotteta (n da), or yama ni nobotta. Keep the ni.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen gomen, tomodachi to yama ni nobotteta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんごめん、友達と山に登ってたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, sorry! I was off climbing a mountain with some friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi ni, tomodachi to yama ni nobotta n da. ue made sanjikan mo kakatta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日に、友達と山に登ったんだ。上まで三時間もかかったよ。
modelAnswers.english: I climbed a mountain with friends on Saturday. It took three whole hours to reach the top.

questions.explanation: Satou-san had planned yama ni noboru tsumori (line 3), says they'll climb ano yama ni noboru next Saturday (line 8), and plans to go fishing again yama ni nobotte kara (after the climb, line 11). English 'climb a mountain' pulls you towards yama o noboru, which is also heard when the way up is the point (a steep path), but for having been up a mountain ni is about three times as common. noboremasu in line 9 is the can-do form: toshi o totta watashi demo noboremasu, even an old man like me can climb it. nobotteta is 'was climbing', a natural excuse for not answering.

questions.english: When rain stopped the climb, what did Satou-san and his friends do instead?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんたちは、代わりに何をしましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんたちは、かわりになにをしましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san-tachi wa, kawari ni nani o shimashita ka?

choices.english: They climbed a smaller mountain nearby.
They went fishing and caught enough for dinner.
They went fishing, but nobody caught anything.

questions.explanation: Line 4: sorede, kawari ni tsuri ni itta n desu (so we went fishing instead), then nanimo tsuremasen deshita (we didn't catch a thing). tsuri ni iku puts the activity straight before ni iku, and tsureru is a fish getting caught on the line, so the negative means nothing bit. B misses that negative. A: nobody climbed anything; rain called off the climb (line 3), and they'll try the same mountain next Saturday (line 8), with fishing again afterwards (mata tsuri ni iku tsumori, line 11).

questions.english: What did Satou-san say Kenta hadn't done for three years?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、ケンタくんのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、けんたくんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, kenta-kun no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He hasn't been camping in three whole years.
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai

choices.english: He hasn't gone 'camping' in three whole years (the English -ing word).
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo kyanpingu ni ittenai

choices.english: He hasn't been fishing in three whole years.
choices.romaji: mou sannen mo tsuri ni ittenai

questions.explanation: Line 6: sou ieba kenta-kun, mou sannen mo kyanpu ni ittenai tte, ittemashita yo ne. ittenai is itte (i)nai, haven't gone, and Satou-san says the same of his own trip in line 2: kyanpu ni itteta n desu (I was away camping). B copies the English '-ing': the activity is kyanpu, and kyanpingu turns up mostly in compounds like kyanpingu kaa (camper van). C: fishing is what Satou-san did on his trip and plans for next Saturday; what Kenta hadn't done in three years was camp, which is why his tent was free to lend.

newWords.english: (of a fish) be caught, bite: nanimo tsuremasen deshita = we didn't catch a thing
name suffix for a younger man or boy (kenta-kun)

83.title: Tanaka-san dresses up

questions.english: Why has Tanaka-san come in dressed up today?

questions.explanation: Line 15: kyou de kekkon shite juu nen (today makes ten years since he married), and line 17: konban wa tsuma to deeto (a date with his wife tonight), so he dressed up a little (chotto kakko tsukete mimashita). Yuki's guess of a date was right, just not the way she meant it. A: kekkon is his own marriage, not a friend's wedding. B: nobody mentions a client or a meeting.

questions.english: Mai tells Yuki what Tanaka-san came in wearing this morning. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは、今朝の田中さんについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、けさのたなかさんについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, kesa no tanaka-san ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He came in wearing a hat (kiru, the clothes verb).
choices.romaji: boushi kite kita no

choices.english: He came in with a hat on (kaburu).
choices.romaji: boushi kabutte kita no

choices.english: He came in with a hat put on (tsukeru).
choices.romaji: boushi tsukete kita no

questions.explanation: Line 3: 'boushi kabutte kita no', and Yuki echoes it in line 4: boushi kaburu n da. Anything pulled over the head (a hat, a cap, a helmet) takes kaburu. A: kiru is for clothes on the body, like a shirt or a coat, so boushi o kiru is the English 'wear' carried over. C: tsukeru is for things put onto the body, like the perfume he also had on (kousui tsuketeta), not for a hat.

questions.english: Yuki says she's never seen Tanaka-san wear a ring. What does Mai tell her?
questions.ja: マイさんは、田中さんの指輪について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、たなかさんのゆびわについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, tanaka-san no yubiwa ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Today he's wearing his ring, too.
He's bought a ring to give his wife tonight.
He's left his ring at home again today.

questions.explanation: Line 11: 'sore ga ne, kyou wa yubiwa mo shiteru no': today he has his ring on as well as the hat, tie and perfume. yubiwa shiteru means the ring is on his finger; nothing is said about buying one (B) or leaving it at home (C). Mai says it to him in line 16 too: dakara yubiwa mo shite kita n desu ne (so that's why you came in wearing your ring).

questions.english: A few days later Tanaka-san is back in his usual open-necked shirt. He has to meet someone important tomorrow, and he asks you, "ashita, daiji na hito ni au n desu kedo, kore de daijoubu deshou ka?" Suggest, politely, that he wear a tie.
questions.ja: 明日、大事な人に会うんですけど、これで大丈夫でしょうか？
questions.kana: あした、だいじなひとにあうんですけど、これでだいじょうぶでしょうか？
questions.romaji: ashita, daiji na hito ni au n desu kedo, kore de daijoubu deshou ka?
questions.answer: Suggest a tie with nekutai o suru, politely since he's your manager: nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu, or nekutai shite kitara dou desu ka? A tie takes suru, never kiru.

modelAnswers.romaji: ichiou, nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 一応、ネクタイをして行ったほうがいいと思います。
modelAnswers.english: I think you'd better wear a tie, just in case.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita mo nekutai shite kitara dou desu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: 明日もネクタイしてきたらどうですか？
modelAnswers.english: Why not wear a tie again tomorrow?

questions.explanation: A tie, like a ring or a watch, takes suru: nekutai shite iku is 'go wearing a tie', nekutai shite kuru 'come in wearing one'. In the scene: nekutai mo shiteru no (line 5) and kyou wa nekutai shiteru n desu ne (line 14). nekutai o kiru is the English 'wear' carried over; kiru is only for clothes on the body.

questions.english: You've just got to the office. Mai leans over and says, "are, nanka ii nioi suru ne." Tell her you've got perfume on.
questions.ja: あれ、なんかいい匂いするね。
questions.kana: あれ、なんかいいにおいするね。
questions.romaji: are, nanka ii nioi suru ne.
questions.answer: Say you're wearing perfume with kousui o tsukeru: kousui tsuketeru (it's on) or kousui tsukete kita (I put some on before I came). Not kousui o kiru.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kousui tsuketeru kara kamo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、香水つけてるからかも。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, maybe it's my perfume.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa chotto kousui tsukete kita n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はちょっと香水つけてきたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I put on a bit of perfume today.

questions.explanation: Perfume takes tsukeru, the verb for anything put onto the body, and tsuketeru means it's on, not that you're putting it on now. In the scene: kousui mo tsuketeta (line 7) and kousui tsukeru nante (line 8). kiru is only for clothes.

84.title: A job close to home
84.setting: Lunchtime at the office in late March. Mai (Kimura-san at work) is about to heat up her packed lunch in the kitchenette microwave when her manager, Tanaka-san, comes in with news about his son, who has spent the past year job hunting.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, tanaka-san, otsukaresama desu. saki ni obentou o atatamete mo ii desu ka?
lines.ja: あ、田中さん、お疲れさまです。先にお弁当を温めてもいいですか？
lines.kana: あ、たなかさん、おつかれさまです。さきにおべんとうをあたためてもいいですか？
lines.english: Oh, hi, Tanaka-san. Mind if I heat up my lunch first?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: douzo. a, kimura-san, uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo.
lines.ja: どうぞ。あ、木村さん、うちの息子、やっと仕事が見つかったんですよ。
lines.kana: どうぞ。あ、きむらさん、うちのむすこ、やっとしごとがみつかったんですよ。
lines.english: Go ahead. Oh, Kimura-san, guess what: my son's finally found a job!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: waa, omedetou gozaimasu! kyonen kara zutto shigoto o sagashiteta n desu yo ne.
lines.ja: わあ、おめでとうございます！去年からずっと仕事を探してたんですよね。
lines.kana: わあ、おめでとうございます！きょねんからずっとしごとをさがしてたんですよね。
lines.english: Oh, congratulations! He'd been looking for a job since last year, hadn't he?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee. ichinen mo shigoto sagashite, nakanaka mitsukaranakatta n desu.
lines.ja: ええ。一年も仕事探して、なかなか見つからなかったんです。
lines.kana: ええ。いちねんもしごとさがして、なかなかみつからなかったんです。
lines.english: Yes. A whole year of job hunting, and nothing would turn up.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: shigoto ga mitsukatte, honto ni yokatta desu ne. doko no kaisha ni hairu n desu ka?
lines.ja: 仕事が見つかって、ほんとによかったですね。どこの会社に入るんですか？
lines.kana: しごとがみつかって、ほんとによかったですね。どこのかいしゃにはいるんですか？
lines.english: I'm so glad he's found one. Which company is he joining?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore ga, raigetsu kara, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu.
lines.ja: それが、来月から、うちの会社に入るんです。
lines.kana: それが、らいげつから、うちのかいしゃにはいるんです。
lines.english: Well, that's the thing. Next month he's joining our company.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, kono kaisha ni desu ka? zenzen shirimasen deshita.
lines.ja: え、この会社にですか？全然知りませんでした。
lines.kana: え、このかいしゃにですか？ぜんぜんしりませんでした。
lines.english: What, this company? I had no idea.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: watashi mo kinou made shiranakatta n desu yo. musuko ga jibun de shigoto o sagashite, watashi ni wa nanimo iwanakatta n desu.
lines.ja: 私も昨日まで知らなかったんですよ。息子が自分で仕事を探して、私には何も言わなかったんです。
lines.kana: わたしもきのうまでしらなかったんですよ。むすこがじぶんでしごとをさがして、わたしにはなにもいわなかったんです。
lines.english: Neither did I, until yesterday. He looked for work all on his own and never said a word to me.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sugoi desu ne. musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka?
lines.ja: すごいですね。息子さんが大学に入ったの、この間じゃなかったですか？
lines.kana: すごいですね。むすこさんがだいがくにはいったの、このあいだじゃなかったですか？
lines.english: Good for him. Didn't he only just start university the other day?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: ee, hayai desu ne. demo, daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari de, shigoto no keiken ga zenzen nai n desu.
lines.ja: ええ、早いですね。でも、大学に入ってから勉強ばっかりで、仕事の経験が全然ないんです。
lines.kana: ええ、はやいですね。でも、だいがくにはいってからべんきょうばっかりで、しごとのけいけんがぜんぜんないんです。
lines.english: Yes, time flies. But since he started university it's been nothing but studying, so he's got no work experience at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: daijoubu desu yo. saisho kara keiken ga aru hito wa, hotondo imasen kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫ですよ。最初から経験がある人は、ほとんどいませんから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶですよ。さいしょからけいけんがあるひとは、ほとんどいませんから。
lines.english: He'll be fine. Hardly anyone has experience at the start.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou deshou ka. kimura-san mo, saisho wa keiken ga nakatta n desu ka?
lines.ja: そうでしょうか。木村さんも、最初は経験がなかったんですか？
lines.kana: そうでしょうか。きむらさんも、さいしょはけいけんがなかったんですか？
lines.english: You think so? So you had no experience at first either, Kimura-san?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: hai. kono kaisha ni haitta toki wa, nanimo dekinakute, mainichi haji o kaite imashita.
lines.ja: はい。この会社に入ったときは、何もできなくて、毎日恥をかいていました。
lines.kana: はい。このかいしゃにはいったときは、なにもできなくて、まいにちはじをかいていました。
lines.english: That's right. When I joined this company I couldn't do a thing, and I was making a fool of myself every day.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou deshita ka? demo ima wa, minna, wakaranai koto wa kimura-san ni kiite imasu yo.
lines.ja: そうでしたか？でも今は、みんな、わからないことは木村さんに聞いていますよ。
lines.kana: そうでしたか？でもいまは、みんな、わからないことはきむらさんにきいていますよ。
lines.english: Were you? Well, these days everyone comes to you when they don't know something.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sonna koto nai desu yo. musuko-san ga komatte itara, watashi mo iroiro oshiemasu ne.
lines.ja: そんなことないですよ。息子さんが困っていたら、私もいろいろ教えますね。
lines.kana: そんなことないですよ。むすこさんがこまっていたら、わたしもいろいろおしえますね。
lines.english: Oh, not really. If your son ever gets stuck, I'll help him out too.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. a, demo, watashi no musuko da tte koto wa, mada minna ni iwanaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。あ、でも、私の息子だってことは、まだみんなに言わないでくださいね。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。あ、でも、わたしのむすこだってことは、まだみんなにいわないでくださいね。
lines.english: Thank you. Oh, but please don't tell anyone yet that he's my son.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, nande desu ka?
lines.ja: え、なんでですか？
lines.kana: え、なんでですか？
lines.english: Oh? Why not?

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: jibun de haitta kaisha da kara iwanaide tte, musuko ni iwareta n desu.
lines.ja: 自分で入った会社だから言わないでって、息子に言われたんです。
lines.kana: じぶんではいったかいしゃだからいわないでって、むすこにいわれたんです。
lines.english: My son told me not to. He got into this company on his own, he says.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Tanaka-san's son is still looking for work after a year, so Tanaka-san asks Mai whether their company might take him on.
Tanaka-san's son has just got into university, and Mai offers to help him get some work experience before he starts.
Tanaka-san's son has finally found a job, at their own company, and Tanaka-san asks Mai to keep quiet for now that he's his son.

questions.explanation: Line 2: uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo. Line 6: the job is at their own company, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu. Lines 16-18: Tanaka-san asks Mai not to tell anyone yet that he's his son, because his son wants it known he got in on his own. A: the son did spend a year looking (line 4), but the search is over. B: university only comes up as Mai remembering when he started (line 9); he's finishing now, and the experience talk is Tanaka-san worrying that he has none (line 10).

questions.english: At Yuki's birthday party, her manager Tanaka-san makes small talk: "What kind of work are you doing at the moment?" Tell him that, actually, you're looking for a job right now.
questions.ja: 今、どんなお仕事をしているんですか？
questions.kana: いま、どんなおしごとをしているんですか？
questions.romaji: ima, donna oshigoto o shite iru n desu ka?
questions.answer: Say you're job hunting with shigoto o sagasu in the -te iru form, politely: jitsu wa, ima shigoto o sagashite iru n desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: jitsu wa, ima shigoto o sagashite iru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 実は、今仕事を探しているんです。
modelAnswers.english: Actually, I'm looking for a job right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: ima wa, atarashii shigoto o sagashite imasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 今は、新しい仕事を探しています。
modelAnswers.english: At the moment I'm looking for a new job.

questions.explanation: Looking for work is shigoto o sagasu, and an ongoing search takes -te iru: sagashite iru, or sagashiteru in casual speech. Mai uses it about Tanaka-san's son, kyonen kara zutto shigoto o sagashiteta n desu yo ne (line 3), Tanaka-san adds ichinen mo shigoto sagashite (line 4), and his son found the job jibun de shigoto o sagashite, looking on his own (line 8). Sagasu is only the looking: once the search is over, the job takes ga, shigoto ga mitsukaru.

questions.english: Mai asks you: "Oh yeah, how's the job thing going? Are you still looking?" Tell her no, you've finally found a job.
questions.ja: そういえば、仕事どう？まだ探してるの？
questions.kana: そういえば、しごとどう？まださがしてるの？
questions.romaji: sou ieba, shigoto dou? mada sagashiteru no?
questions.answer: Say the search is over with shigoto ga mitsukaru in the past: uun, yatto shigoto mitsukatta n da!

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, yatto shigoto mitsukatta n da!
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、やっと仕事見つかったんだ！
modelAnswers.english: No, I finally found a job!

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, sengetsu atarashii shigoto ga mitsukatta n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、先月新しい仕事が見つかったんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I found a new job last month.

questions.explanation: Finding work is shigoto ga mitsukaru: the job is what turns up, so it takes ga, not the o of sagasu. Tanaka-san's news is uchi no musuko, yatto shigoto ga mitsukatta n desu yo (line 2), and Mai answers shigoto ga mitsukatte, honto ni yokatta desu ne (line 5). Mai's question uses sagasu for the looking; your answer switches both the verb and the particle. Casual speech can drop ga, as in the first model answer.

questions.english: Mai remembers when Tanaka-san's son started university. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは、息子さんについて何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、むすこさんについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, musuko-san ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: that he started university (got in)
choices.romaji: daigaku ni haitta

choices.english: that he began university (English 'start' word for word)
choices.romaji: daigaku o hajimeta

choices.english: that he went to the university
choices.romaji: daigaku ni itta

questions.explanation: Mai says musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka? (line 9), and Tanaka-san picks it up: daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari (line 10). You enter a school, so starting university is daigaku ni hairu, the same ni hairu as kaisha ni hairu. B puts English 'start university' into Japanese word for word, and nobody says it. C, daigaku ni itta, means he went there, to the campus or to classes, not that he got in.

questions.english: Tanaka-san's news is that his son will uchi no kaisha ni hairu from next month. What does that mean?
questions.ja: 田中さんの息子さんは、来月から何をしますか？
questions.kana: たなかさんのむすこさんは、らいげつからなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no musuko-san wa, raigetsu kara nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: He'll come into the office with his dad now and then to see what the work is like.
He'll join their company and start working there as a new employee.
He'll take part in a short work-experience event that their company runs.

questions.explanation: Line 6: sore ga, raigetsu kara, uchi no kaisha ni hairu n desu. Kaisha ni hairu is joining a company as a member of staff: Mai uses it for her own start, kono kaisha ni haitta toki (line 13), and the son wants it known he got in on his own, jibun de haitta kaisha (line 18). Going in to the office is kaisha ni iku or kuru (A), and taking part in an event is sanka suru (C), the word English 'join' tempts you into.

questions.english: Tanaka-san, your manager, asks: "Could I ask you to take on this job? It's a little tricky." Tell him it's fine, because you have experience with this kind of work.
questions.ja: この仕事、お願いしてもいいですか？ちょっと難しいんですけど。
questions.kana: このしごと、おねがいしてもいいですか？ちょっとむずかしいんですけど。
questions.romaji: kono shigoto, onegai shite mo ii desu ka? chotto muzukashii n desu kedo.
questions.answer: Say you have the background with keiken ga aru, politely keiken ga arimasu, not keiken o motte imasu: kou iu shigoto no keiken wa arimasu kara, daijoubu desu.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, kou iu shigoto no keiken wa arimasu kara, daijoubu desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、こういう仕事の経験はありますから、大丈夫です。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. I've done this kind of work before, so it's fine.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu desu. mae ni mo onaji shigoto o shita keiken ga arimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫です。前にも同じ仕事をした経験があります。
modelAnswers.english: No problem. I've done the same work before.

questions.explanation: Experience is something that exists, so it takes ga aru: keiken ga aru, or keiken ga arimasu to your manager. Tanaka-san worries his son has none, shigoto no keiken ga zenzen nai n desu (line 10); Mai answers saisho kara keiken ga aru hito wa, hotondo imasen (line 11); and Tanaka-san asks her, saisho wa keiken ga nakatta n desu ka? (line 12). Keiken o motte imasu is English 'have experience' word for word and sounds like a line read off a CV. Wa in place of ga (keiken wa arimasu) is fine when you mean this kind of work, at least.

86.title: Blossoms Twice
86.setting: A Sunday in early March at the family home. Yuki, who lives on her own, has dropped by and asks her little brother Kenji, who finishes high school this month, about the university in Hokkaido he starts at in April.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenji, hokkaidou no daigaku ni hairu n da tte? nande hokkaidou ni shita no?
lines.ja: ケンジ、北海道の大学に入るんだって？なんで北海道にしたの？
lines.kana: けんじ、ほっかいどうのだいがくにはいるんだって？なんでほっかいどうにしたの？
lines.english: Kenji, I hear you're going to university in Hokkaido? Why Hokkaido?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: atsusa ni yowai kara. kotchi no natsu, mou muri.
lines.ja: 暑さに弱いから。こっちの夏、もう無理。
lines.kana: あつさによわいから。こっちのなつ、もうむり。
lines.english: 'Cause I can't take the heat. I'm done with summers here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sore dake? maa, kenji wa mukashi kara atsusa ni yowai kedo.
lines.ja: え、それだけ？まあ、ケンジは昔から暑さに弱いけど。
lines.kana: え、それだけ？まあ、けんじはむかしからあつさによわいけど。
lines.english: What, that's it? I mean, you've always been hopeless in the heat, but still.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi. nanimo shinakute mo ase kaku shi.
lines.ja: 朝からセミが鳴いて、寝られないし。何もしなくても汗かくし。
lines.kana: あさからせみがないて、ねられないし。なにもしなくてもあせかくし。
lines.english: The cicadas start up first thing, so I can't sleep. And I sweat even doing nothing.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ee, semi ga naku to, natsu tte kanji de ii jan.
lines.ja: えー、セミが鳴くと、夏って感じでいいじゃん。
lines.kana: えー、せみがなくと、なつってかんじでいいじゃん。
lines.english: Aw, but when the cicadas start, it really feels like summer. I like that.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: atchi wa, semi anmari nakanai rashii yo. natsu mo sonna ni atsukunai tte.
lines.ja: あっちは、セミあんまり鳴かないらしいよ。夏もそんなに暑くないって。
lines.kana: あっちは、せみあんまりなかないらしいよ。なつもそんなにあつくないって。
lines.english: Apparently the cicadas don't go much up there. And summer's not that hot either.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo, fuyu wa? atchi, yuki sugoku tsumoru yo.
lines.ja: でも、冬は？あっち、雪すごく積もるよ。
lines.kana: でも、ふゆは？あっち、ゆきすごくつもるよ。
lines.english: But what about winter? The snow really piles up there.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shitteru. yuki ga tsumoru no, chotto tanoshimi.
lines.ja: 知ってる。雪が積もるの、ちょっと楽しみ。
lines.kana: しってる。ゆきがつもるの、ちょっとたのしみ。
lines.english: I know. I'm kind of looking forward to the snow piling up.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yuki wa futteru dake nara kirei da kedo, tsumoru to taihen da yo.
lines.ja: 雪は降ってるだけならきれいだけど、積もると大変だよ。
lines.kana: ゆきはふってるだけならきれいだけど、つもるとたいへんだよ。

lines.speaker: kenji

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenji is going to university in Hokkaido, partly because he can't take the heat. Lines 13-15: the cherry blossoms come out about a month later up there, so Yuki says she'll visit when they do (atchi de sakura ga saitara, asobi ni iku) and get to see them twice this year. A is wrong: Kenji asks her to come and help when the snow piles up (line 16), but she says no, because she can't take the cold herself (line 17). C is wrong: Yuki teases him about the cold (line 11), but she never tries to change his mind.

questions.english: It's early April. Kenji has moved to Hokkaido, where the cherry blossoms won't be out for weeks. He calls and asks, "sotchi, sakura dou?" (how are the blossoms there?). The ones near you are out. Tell him, using saku.
questions.ja: そっち、桜どう？
questions.kana: そっち、さくらどう？
questions.romaji: sotchi, sakura dou?
questions.answer: Say they're out with saiteru: mou saiteru yo (they're already out). Saita says they've come out, saiteru says they're out now, and mada saitenai is not out yet. Don't reach for deru: hana ga deru isn't said.

modelAnswers.romaji: mou saiteru yo. ima ga ichiban kirei.
