questions.explanation: Yuki and Kenji use saku for the blossoms in lines 13 to 15: atchi tte sakura ga saku no, osoi n da yo ne? (they come out late up there, don't they?), osoku saku tte (they come out later), and atchi de sakura ga saitara (when they come out up there). Flowers coming out is saku, and flowers that are out now are saiteru. English 'the blossoms are out' tempts deru, but hana ga deru isn't said, and hiraku (open) is for describing petals, not for chat. When the petals come down, it's chiru: mou chitchatta. In casual talk ga usually drops: sakura saita?

questions.english: It's a scorching day in August. Yuki suggests eating lunch outside: "ohiru, soto de tabenai?" Say no: you just can't take the heat. Use atsusa ni yowai.
questions.ja: お昼、外で食べない？
questions.kana: おひる、そとでたべない？
questions.romaji: ohiru, soto de tabenai?
questions.answer: Explain with atsusa ni yowai, often as atsusa ni yowai n da (the thing is, I'm no good in the heat). Keep the ni: atsusa ga yowai would mean the heat itself is weak.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, atsusa ni yowai n da. naka de tabenai?
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、暑さに弱いんだ。中で食べない？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I can't take the heat. Can we eat inside?

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa chotto. atsusa ni yowai kara, naka ni shiyou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日はちょっと。暑さに弱いから、中にしようよ。
modelAnswers.english: Not today. I'm no good in the heat, so let's eat inside.

questions.explanation: Kenji's reason for Hokkaido is atsusa ni yowai kara (line 2), Yuki agrees he always has been (line 3), and he sets it against the cold in line 10: atsusa ni wa yowai kedo, samusa ni wa yowakunai. Yuki turns it round on him at the end: samusa ni yowai kara (line 17). Yowai with ni means you can't handle something, like osake ni yowai (can't hold your drink), and with atsusa the ni stays, never ga. Atsusa and samusa are atsui and samui made into nouns with -sa. Atsui no nigate (I can't do heat) is just as everyday; the opposite is atsusa ni tsuyoi.

questions.explanation: Line 4: asa kara semi ga naite, nerarenai shi. Insects, birds and animals all naku (鳴く), which sounds the same as naku 'cry' (泣く): semi ga naku, tori ga naku, neko ga naku. A carries the English verb over: utau is singing a song, and tori ga utau is poetry, not chat. B uses naru, which is for things that make a sound, like denwa ga naru or kaminari ga naru: animals naku, things naru. Yuki says it too (line 5: semi ga naku to, natsu tte kanji), and Kenji again in line 6 (semi anmari nakanai).

questions.explanation: Line 7: atchi, yuki sugoku tsumoru yo (the snow really piles up there). Line 9: futteru dake nara kirei da kedo, tsumoru to taihen da yo (pretty while it's coming down, hard work once it settles). Furu is snow coming down; tsumoru is snow building up and staying, so yuki tsumotteru means there's snow on the ground. B is wrong: she says a lot of it piles up. C is wrong: snow that tsumoru stays put; snow melting is tokeru. Snow stuck on things, like a car, is tsuku: kuruma ni yuki ga tsuiteru.

edits.value: kono aida mitai ni, nekutai shite itta hou ga ii kamo shiremasen ne.
edits.why: The old model, ashita mo nekutai shite kitara dou desu ka?, uses -tara dou desu ka. Said to your own manager, that sounds pushy, and the cue asks for a polite suggestion. The new model softens it with kamo shiremasen and recalls the tie he wore the other day.

edits.why: Keeps the ja in step with the new romaji.

edits.value: Suggest a tie with nekutai o suru, politely since he's your manager: nekutai o shite itta hou ga ii to omoimasu, or more softly, nekutai shite itta hou ga ii kamo shiremasen ne. Skip -tara dou desu ka with a manager, as it can sound pushy. A tie takes suru, never kiru.
edits.why: The answer quoted the dropped -tara dou desu ka model. It now matches the new model answers and gives the register point.

edits.value: daigaku o haitta
edits.why: The old wrong choice, daigaku ni itta, means 'went to university' (started going), which is just as natural in Mai's line. So the heard question had two acceptable answers. Swapping in o for ni gives the common learner slip that the chunk's mix-up note warns about (daigaku takes ni hairu).

edits.value: that he entered university (with o, like English 'enter')
edits.why: A gloss for the new wrong choice, in the same style as the other two choices.

edits.value: Mai says musuko-san ga daigaku ni haitta no, kono aida ja nakatta desu ka? (line 9), and Tanaka-san picks it up: daigaku ni haitte kara benkyou bakkari (line 10). You go into a school, so starting university is daigaku ni hairu, with ni for the place you go into, the same ni hairu as kaisha ni hairu. B puts English 'start university' into Japanese word for word, and nobody says it. C copies English 'enter university' with o, but hairu takes ni for what you join: daigaku o haitta is a common learner slip.

87.title: A dog bed for the cat
87.setting: Saturday morning at the door of Yuki's small rented flat. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, turns up with a big parcel of hers that the driver took to his flat by mistake last night.

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?

questions.kana: なにがありましたか？

choices.english: The dog bed Yuki ordered for the small dog she's getting turns out to be for a big dog, so it goes to Satou-san's cat, and she'll buy a small one once the dog has come.
Yuki finds out dogs aren't allowed in her rented flat, so Satou-san offers to keep the dog at his place.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: Satou-san brings round Yuki's parcel, which went to his flat by mistake. It's a dog bed, because she's getting a dog next week (raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu). Lines 11-12: when she takes it out, it's a bed for a big dog, and she realises she ordered the wrong one (machigaete tanonjatta). Line 14: a big dog won't work in her cramped flat. Lines 15-16: Satou-san asks for the bed for his cat, Tama, and Yuki will buy a small one after the dog comes and she's seen how it settles in (yousu o mite). B is wrong: when Yuki rented the flat she was told a small dog would be fine (line 6), and Satou-san never offers to keep the dog. C swaps them round: it's Yuki's parcel (yuki-san no nimotsu, line 1), and the bed goes from Yuki to Satou-san's cat, not the other way.

questions.english: Satou-san asks if Yuki's allowed to keep a dog where she lives. What does she say?

questions.explanation: Line 6: kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita. Japanese has no separate verb for renting a place: the tenant kariru (borrows), the same verb as borrowing a pen. Satou-san uses it for the poky room he had years ago (semai heya o karite, line 7), and Yuki says a big dog would mean renting somewhere roomier (motto hiroi heya o karinai to, line 14). A is wrong: kasu (lend) is the landlord's side, so heya o kasu toki would mean when she let the flat out to someone else. B is wrong: rentaru suru is for hiring things like a car or a kimono for a day, not a flat you live in.

questions.english: You've just moved into a new flat, and Kenta has come round for the first time. At the door he says, "hee, koko ga atarashii heya? haitte ii?" (Oh, so this is the new place? Can I come in?) Invite him in the modest way a host does, saying it's a small place.
questions.ja: へえ、ここが新しい部屋？入っていい？
questions.kana: へえ、ここがあたらしいへや？はいっていい？
questions.romaji: hee, koko ga atarashii heya? haitte ii?
questions.answer: Use the host's set line with semai heya: semai heya da kedo, douzo (it's a tiny place, but come in).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, semai heya da kedo, douzo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、狭い部屋だけど、どうぞ。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. It's a tiny place, but come on in.

modelAnswers.romaji: semai heya desu kedo, douzo haitte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: 狭い部屋ですけど、どうぞ入ってください。
modelAnswers.english: It's only a small place, but please, come in.

questions.explanation: Yuki says just this to Satou-san in line 10: semai heya desu kedo, douzo. It's the host's modest welcome, and a guest will often answer hiroi ne! (it's roomy!). A cramped room or flat is semai, the opposite of hiroi, as in line 14 (kono semai heya de desu ka? ... motto hiroi heya). Chiisai heya is fine for a room's size (chiisai heya ga futatsu aru), but for the cramped feeling, and in this welcome, people say semai. Kenta's a friend, so da kedo. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san. Semai tokoro da kedo, douzo is a common variant.

questions.english: Kenta shows you photos of a friend's new puppy and says, "kawaii desho? inu, suki?" (Cute, right? Do you like dogs?) You love dogs, and your family has one at home. Tell him.
questions.ja: かわいいでしょ？犬、好き？
questions.kana: かわいいでしょ？いぬ、すき？
questions.romaji: kawaii desho? inu, suki?
questions.answer: Say you love them, then say your family keeps one with inu o kau in the -teru form: uchi mo inu katteru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daisuki! uchi mo inu katteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大好き！うちも犬飼ってるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I love them! We've got a dog at home too.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, daisuki desu. uchi de mo inu o katte iru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、大好きです。うちでも犬を飼っているんです。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I love them. We have a dog at home too.

questions.explanation: Keeping a pet is kau, which sounds just like kau 'buy'. Yuki uses it for the dog she's getting (raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu, line 4), and Satou-san for the dog he had years ago (inu o katte imashita, line 7). His nanika katta n desu ka? in line 3 is the other kau, 'buy', and the context keeps them apart. Having a pet is almost always in the -teru form: inu katteru. Inu o motte iru sounds like you own a dog the way you own a bag, and inu ga iru (there's a dog) also works. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

questions.english: Satou-san brings Yuki her parcel. What had happened to it?
questions.ja: ユキさんの荷物は、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんのにもつは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san no nimotsu wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki was out when it came last night, so the driver left it with Satou-san next door.
The driver took it to Satou-san's flat by mistake last night, so it never reached Yuki, though she'd waited in all day.
It was left outside Yuki's door last night, and Satou-san took it in so it wouldn't go missing.

questions.explanation: Line 1: kinou no yoru, yuki-san no nimotsu ga uchi ni todoita n desu yo. heya o machigaeta mitai de. Todoku means 'reach', and here the parcel reached the wrong flat. Line 2: Yuki waited in all day, but nimotsu ga todokanakute (it never reached her). Things sent to you todoku, the same verb as for letters and messages. Tsuku is for people and trains getting somewhere (eki ni tsuku), so nimotsu ga tsuita is less usual. A is wrong: Yuki was in, waiting all day (zutto matteta), and the driver got the flat wrong. C is wrong: it never got to Yuki's door. It was delivered straight to Satou-san's place (uchi ni todoita).

88.title: The same worry
88.setting: A quiet weekday evening at the café where Sora works part-time. Mai, a regular, has been sitting alone over her coffee looking down, so Sora comes over to her table.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mai-san, genki nai ne. nanka nayami aru no?
lines.ja: マイさん、元気ないね。なんか悩みあるの？
lines.kana: まいさん、げんきないね。なんかなやみあるの？
lines.english: Mai, you look a bit down. Is something on your mind?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. sora-kun, ima ii? chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo.
lines.ja: うん。ソラくん、今いい？ちょっと相談があるんだけど。
lines.kana: うん。そらくん、いまいい？ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。
lines.english: Yeah. Sora, have you got a minute? I could use your advice on something.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii yo, ima hima da shi. boku de yokattara, soudan noru yo.
lines.ja: いいよ、今ひまだし。僕でよかったら、相談乗るよ。
lines.kana: いいよ、いまひまだし。ぼくでよかったら、そうだんのるよ。
lines.english: Sure, it's quiet right now anyway. If I can help, I'm all ears.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou. kondo no shuumatsu, yuki to kyanpu ni iku no.
lines.ja: ありがとう。今度の週末、ユキとキャンプに行くの。
lines.kana: ありがとう。こんどのしゅうまつ、ゆきときゃんぷにいくの。
lines.english: Thanks. Yuki and I are going camping this weekend.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: hee, ii ne. demo, tanoshimi ja nai no? honne itte ii yo.
lines.ja: へえ、いいね。でも、楽しみじゃないの？本音言っていいよ。
lines.kana: へえ、いいね。でも、たのしみじゃないの？ほんねいっていいよ。
lines.english: Oh, nice. But you're not looking forward to it? You can tell me how you really feel.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honne o iu to, anmari ikitakunai n da. soto de neru no, nigate de.
lines.ja: 本音を言うと、あんまり行きたくないんだ。外で寝るの、苦手で。
lines.kana: ほんねをいうと、あんまりいきたくないんだ。そとでねるの、にがてで。
lines.english: To be honest, I don't really want to go. I'm not great at sleeping outdoors.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sokka. sore, yuki-san ni itta?
lines.ja: そっか。それ、ユキさんに言った？
lines.kana: そっか。それ、ゆきさんにいった？
lines.english: I see. Have you told Yuki?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ienai yo. watashi ga mae ni, kyanpu tanoshisou tte itta kara, yuki ga keikaku tatete kureta no.
lines.ja: 言えないよ。私が前に、キャンプ楽しそうって言ったから、ユキが計画立ててくれたの。
lines.kana: いえないよ。わたしがまえに、きゃんぷたのしそうっていったから、ゆきがけいかくたててくれたの。
lines.english: I can't! I once said camping sounded fun, so Yuki went and planned it for me.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: demo, iwanai to, shuumatsu zutto soto de neru koto ni naru yo. honne, itte mitara?
lines.ja: でも、言わないと、週末ずっと外で寝ることになるよ。本音、言ってみたら？
lines.kana: でも、いわないと、しゅうまつずっとそとでねることになるよ。ほんね、いってみたら？
lines.english: But if you don't, you'll be sleeping outdoors all weekend. Why not tell her how you really feel?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou da yo ne. a, yuki kara renraku kita.
lines.ja: そうだよね。あ、ユキから連絡来た。
lines.kana: そうだよね。あ、ゆきかられんらくきた。
lines.english: You're right. Oh, a message from Yuki.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: nante?
lines.ja: なんて？
lines.kana: なんて？
lines.english: What does she say?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo. honne o iu to, kyanpu nigate na n da tte.
lines.ja: 「ちょっと相談があるんだけど。本音を言うと、キャンプ苦手なんだ」って。
lines.kana: 「ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。ほんねをいうと、きゃんぷにがてなんだ」って。
lines.english: "There's something I want to ask you about. To be honest, I'm not really into camping."

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, yuki-san mo onaji nayami ga atta n da!
lines.ja: え、ユキさんも同じ悩みがあったんだ！
lines.kana: え、ゆきさんもおなじなやみがあったんだ！
lines.english: What? So Yuki had the same worry!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. watashi ga ikitasou datta kara, keikaku tateta n da tte.
lines.ja: うん。私が行きたそうだったから、計画立てたんだって。
lines.kana: うん。わたしがいきたそうだったから、けいかくたてたんだって。
lines.english: Yeah. She says she only planned it because I looked like I wanted to go.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: nan da. jaa, mai-san mo yuki-san mo, ikitakunakatta n da.
lines.ja: なんだ。じゃあ、マイさんもユキさんも、行きたくなかったんだ。
lines.kana: なんだ。じゃあ、まいさんもゆきさんも、いきたくなかったんだ。
lines.english: Ha! So neither of you actually wanted to go.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou mitai. kyanpu wa chuushi ni narisou da kedo, kawari ni yuki to koko ni kuru ne.
lines.ja: そうみたい。キャンプは中止になりそうだけど、かわりにユキとここに来るね。
lines.kana: そうみたい。きゃんぷはちゅうしになりそうだけど、かわりにゆきとここにくるね。
lines.english: Looks like it. The camping trip's probably off, but I'll come here with Yuki instead.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii ne, matteru. mata nayami ga attara, itsudemo soudan ni noru yo.
lines.ja: いいね、待ってる。また悩みがあったら、いつでも相談に乗るよ。
lines.kana: いいね、まってる。またなやみがあったら、いつでもそうだんにのるよ。
lines.english: Great, I'll be here. And if anything's on your mind again, I'm always happy to listen.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: arigatou. sora-kun ni soudan ni notte moratte, yokatta.
lines.ja: ありがとう。ソラくんに相談に乗ってもらって、よかった。
lines.kana: ありがとう。そらくんにそうだんにのってもらって、よかった。
lines.english: Thanks, Sora. I'm really glad I talked it over with you.

questions.english: What happened with Mai's worry?
questions.ja: マイさんの悩みは、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんのなやみは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san no nayami wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Mai was afraid the camping trip would be called off, but Yuki's message says it's still on.
Mai didn't want to go camping but couldn't tell Yuki, then found out Yuki didn't want to go either.
Mai was looking forward to camping, but Yuki admitted she doesn't like it, so now Mai is disappointed.

questions.explanation: Line 6: Mai admits she doesn't really want to go (honne o iu to, anmari ikitakunai n da). Line 8: she can't tell Yuki, who planned the trip because Mai once said camping sounded fun. Lines 12-14: Yuki's message says she doesn't like camping either and only planned it because Mai seemed keen. Line 16: the trip will probably be called off (chuushi ni narisou), and they'll come to the café instead. A is wrong: Mai was dreading the trip, not afraid of losing it, and the message never says it's still on. C is wrong: Mai wasn't looking forward to it (line 6), and she ends up relieved, thanking Sora (line 18), not disappointed.

questions.english: After hearing Yuki's message, Sora says, "yuki-san mo onaji nayami ga atta n da!" What does he mean?
questions.ja: ソラくんは、何がわかりましたか？
questions.kana: そらくんは、なにがわかりましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-kun wa, nani ga wakarimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki had made other plans for the same weekend.
Yuki wants to ask Sora's advice too.
Yuki had been quietly worrying about the same thing as Mai.

questions.explanation: Line 13: nayami ga aru means having something on your mind, a problem you keep turning over, and onaji nayami is the same worry. Yuki didn't want to go camping either (line 12: honne o iu to, kyanpu nigate na n da) but kept it to herself because she thought Mai wanted to go (line 14). Sora uses the same phrase to ask what's wrong in line 1 (nanka nayami aru no?) and to offer help in line 17 (mata nayami ga attara). A mixes it up with having plans (yotei ga aru); nobody mentions other plans. B mixes it up with soudan ga aru: Yuki's message opens with chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo (line 12), but she's asking Mai, not Sora.

questions.english: How does Mai bring up her problem with Sora?
questions.ja: マイさんは、ソラくんに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、そらくんになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, sora-kun ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: there's something I'd like your advice on
choices.romaji: chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo

choices.english: I'm happy to hear you out
choices.romaji: soudan ni noru yo

choices.english: give me some advice, please
choices.romaji: chotto adobaisu kudasai

questions.explanation: Line 2: Mai opens with "chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo", the everyday way to run something by a friend. The one with the problem has a soudan, and the sentence trails off on kedo so the friend can say go ahead. Yuki's message opens the same way in line 12. B is the friend's side: Sora answers with soudan noru yo in line 3, so from Mai it would mean she's offering to hear him out. C is 'give me advice' word for word. adobaisu kudasai sounds abrupt between friends, and asking someone to help you think something through is soudan, not adobaisu.

questions.english: Over dinner, your friend Kenta sighs and says, "saikin, shigoto de iroiro atte sa. chotto tsukarechatta." Offer to hear him out, using soudan ni noru.
questions.ja: 最近、仕事でいろいろあってさ。ちょっと疲れちゃった。
questions.kana: さいきん、しごとでいろいろあってさ。ちょっとつかれちゃった。
questions.romaji: saikin, shigoto de iroiro atte sa. chotto tsukarechatta.
questions.answer: Offer to listen with soudan ni noru, the way Sora does: watashi (or boku) de yokattara, soudan noru yo (if I can help, I'm all ears), or itsudemo soudan ni noru yo (I'm always here to talk).

modelAnswers.romaji: sou na n da. watashi de yokattara, soudan noru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: そうなんだ。私でよかったら、相談乗るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, really? If I can help, I'm all ears.

modelAnswers.romaji: taihen da ne. itsudemo soudan ni noru kara, nandemo itte ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 大変だね。いつでも相談に乗るから、何でも言ってね。
modelAnswers.english: That sounds rough. I'm always here to talk, so tell me anything.

questions.explanation: soudan ni noru is the friend's side. Sora offers it in line 3 (boku de yokattara, soudan noru yo) and line 17 (itsudemo soudan ni noru yo), and Mai thanks him for it in line 18 (soudan ni notte moratte, yokatta). It means hearing someone out and helping them think it through, so adobaisu suru (passing on tips) misses the point. Don't answer with soudan ga aru: that's the side with the problem, the way Mai and Yuki say it (lines 2 and 12). In casual speech the ni often drops (soudan noru yo).

questions.english: Yuki shows you a hat she's just bought: "atarashii boushi katta n da. dou? kawaii desho?" Honestly, you think it looks a bit odd. Tell her what you really think, using honne o iu.
questions.ja: 新しい帽子買ったんだ。どう？かわいいでしょ？
questions.kana: あたらしいぼうしかったんだ。どう？かわいいでしょ？
questions.romaji: atarashii boushi katta n da. dou? kawaii desho?
questions.answer: Open with honne o iu to (to be honest), the way Mai does, then say what you really think and soften it: chotto hen kamo (it might be a bit odd), or say you like her old one better.

modelAnswers.romaji: etto, honne o iu to, chotto hen kamo.
modelAnswers.ja: えっと、本音を言うと、ちょっと変かも。
modelAnswers.english: Um, to be honest, it looks a bit odd.

modelAnswers.romaji: honne o iu to, mae no boushi no hou ga suki kana.
modelAnswers.ja: 本音を言うと、前の帽子のほうが好きかな。
modelAnswers.english: Honestly? I think I like your old hat better.

questions.explanation: honne is what you really feel, behind the polite front (tatemae), and honne o iu to opens a frank admission. Mai uses it in line 6 (honne o iu to, anmari ikitakunai n da), and so does Yuki's message in line 12 (honne o iu to, kyanpu nigate na n da). Sora uses the other everyday form to invite it: honne itte ii yo (line 5) and honne, itte mitara? (line 9). Yuki's kawaii desho? is fishing for the polite answer, and that's why honne fits. shoujiki ni iu to also means 'to be honest', but it's just being frank, not dropping a polite front. Soften what comes next the way Mai does with anmari, using chotto, kamo or kana.

newWords.english: camping, a camping trip (kyanpu ni iku: go camping)

lines.speaker: okaasan

questions.english: What happens while Kenji and Okaasan wait to see the doctor?

questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Okaasan couldn't get away from work, so Kenji waited for the doctor on his own.

questions.explanation: Line 1: there's still an hour to wait (mada ichijikan mo kakaru). In lines 4-5 they go to the café across the road to kill time. Line 8: Okaasan managed to make time in a busy week. In line 12 Kenji says it doesn't hurt any more and he wants to go home. In line 13 she says no: sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara, the doctor looks at it first. A is wrong: Okaasan is right there with him and says she made the time (line 8). C is wrong: she won't go home (line 13). Next week only comes up in case the doctor asks Kenji to come back (lines 14-15).

questions.english: Okaasan explains why the wait is so long. What does she say about the doctor?
questions.ja: お母さんは、先生について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、せんせいについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, sensei ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He spends a full hour with every patient.
He's always running late, so his patients end up waiting.
He takes his time and looks at each patient properly.

questions.explanation: Line 2: 'koko no sensei, hitori hitori chanto jikan kakete mite kureru kara'. Jikan o kakeru is choosing to put time into something, here each patient (hitori hitori), properly (chanto). Kenji grumbles jikan kakesugi da yo (line 3, he takes way too long), and at the end he'll eat his snack slowly: jikan kakete, yukkuri taberu (line 18). A mixes it up with line 1: the hour is how long the wait still takes, mada ichijikan mo kakaru, and kakaru is how long something takes. It isn't time per patient. B is wrong: nobody says he's late. The wait is long because he's thorough.

questions.english: Your manager Tanaka-san stayed after work to go through your presentation with you, even though his week is packed. When you're done, he says, "jaa, kyou wa kono gurai ni shimashou ka." Thank him for making time for you, using jikan o toru.
questions.ja: じゃあ、今日はこのぐらいにしましょうか。
questions.kana: じゃあ、きょうはこのぐらいにしましょうか。
questions.romaji: jaa, kyou wa kono gurai ni shimashou ka.
questions.answer: Thank him politely with jikan o toru: ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita (thank you for making time for me). To apologise for taking up his time, use the causative: ojikan torasete shimatte sumimasen.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai. kyou wa ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: はい。今日はお時間取っていただいて、ありがとうございました。
modelAnswers.english: Yes. Thank you for making time for me today.

modelAnswers.romaji: oisogashii tokoro, ojikan torasete shimatte sumimasen. arigatou gozaimashita.
modelAnswers.ja: お忙しいところ、お時間取らせてしまってすみません。ありがとうございました。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry to take up your time when you're so busy. Thank you.

questions.explanation: Kenji says it to Okaasan in line 10: nanka, jikan totte kurete arigatou. She has just said she hardly ever gets time to talk with him (line 9, nakanaka torenai). Jikan o toru is setting time aside, and it's the usual way to thank someone for theirs. With your manager, make it polite with o- and itadaite: ojikan totte itadaite. The apology uses the causative: ojikan torasete (making you take the time). English 'take' can mislead you, though: how long something takes is kakaru, as in mada ichijikan mo kakaru (line 1). Ojikan tsukutte itadaite would also work, if you want to stress that he squeezed you in.

questions.english: Kenta asks, "konshuu, issho ni nanika tabe ni ikanai?" Your week is packed, but next week looks better. Tell him you can make time next week.
questions.ja: 今週、一緒に何か食べに行かない？
questions.kana: こんしゅう、いっしょになにかたべにいかない？
questions.romaji: konshuu, issho ni nanika tabe ni ikanai?
questions.answer: Use jikan o tsukuru in the potential: raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo (I can make time next week). Saying konshuu wa chotto isogashii kedo first softens the no.

modelAnswers.romaji: konshuu wa chotto isogashii kedo, raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 今週はちょっと忙しいけど、来週なら時間作れるよ。
modelAnswers.english: This week's a bit busy, but I can make time next week.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, konshuu wa muri. raishuu nara, nantoka jikan tsukuru kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今週は無理。来週なら、なんとか時間作るから。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, this week's impossible. I'll find time next week somehow.

questions.explanation: Okaasan uses it three times: nantoka jikan tsukutta (line 8, she managed to make time in a busy week), sekkaku jikan tsukutta n da kara (line 13, I went to the trouble of making time) and raishuu nara, mata jikan tsukureru (line 15, I can make time again next week). 'Make time' really is tsukuru, and as in English it means squeezing time out of a full schedule. Jikan o toru (lines 9-10) is setting it aside. The potential, jikan tsukureru, is how you promise to fit someone in. With a friend, casual is right.

questions.english: There's another hour to wait. What did Okaasan suggest?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Shall we kill some time at the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka

choices.english: Shall we murder some time at the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan korosou ka

choices.english: Shall we put some time into the café across the road?
choices.romaji: mae no kafe de jikan kakeyou ka

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'jaa, mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka'. Kenji answers nanika tabenagara jikan tsubusou (line 5), and later mou hitotsu tabete, jikan tsubusou kana (line 16). Killing time is tsubusu, 'squash': you squash the empty time flat. B is a word-for-word copy of 'kill time'. Korosu is only for killing living things, so jikan o korosu sounds like a murder plot. C is wrong: jikan o kakeru is putting time into something on purpose, like the doctor with each patient (line 2). Here they just want to fill a wait.

90.title: The idea from the bath
90.setting: Monday afternoon at the office. On Friday, Tanaka-san asked Yuki for an idea for the next campaign, and he wants it today. Her coworker and friend Mai (Kimura-san at work) sits at the next desk.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: yuki-san, sengetsu no kyanpeen, kekka ga demashita yo. amari yokunakatta desu ne.
lines.ja: ユキさん、先月のキャンペーン、結果が出ましたよ。あまり良くなかったですね。
lines.kana: ゆきさん、せんげつのきゃんぺーん、けっかがでましたよ。あまりよくなかったですね。
lines.english: Yuki-san, last month's campaign results are in. I'm afraid they weren't very good.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. kondo koso, kekka o dashitai desu ne.
lines.ja: そうですか。今度こそ、結果を出したいですね。
lines.kana: そうですか。こんどこそ、けっかをだしたいですね。
lines.english: I see. This time I really want to get results.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kin'youbi ni tanonda aidea, kyoujuu ni onegai shimasu ne. ii aidea nara, sugu hanko o oshimasu kara.
lines.ja: 金曜日に頼んだアイデア、今日中にお願いしますね。いいアイデアなら、すぐハンコを押しますから。
lines.kana: きんようびにたのんだあいであ、きょうじゅうにおねがいしますね。いいあいであなら、すぐはんこをおしますから。
lines.english: The idea I asked you for on Friday: I'd like it by the end of today. If it's a good one, I'll put my stamp on it straight away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo. asa kara zutto atama tsukatteru noni, zenzen ii aidea ga ukabanai no.
lines.ja: マイ、ちょっと相談があるんだけど。朝からずっと頭使ってるのに、全然いいアイデアが浮かばないの。
lines.kana: まい、ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。あさからずっとあたまつかってるのに、ぜんぜんいいあいであがうかばないの。
lines.english: Mai, can I ask your advice? I've been racking my brains all morning, and I can't come up with a single good idea.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: atama tsukaisugi da yo. chotto yasundara?
lines.ja: 頭使いすぎだよ。ちょっと休んだら？
lines.kana: あたまつかいすぎだよ。ちょっとやすんだら？
lines.english: You're thinking too hard. Why not take a little break?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: datte, kinou ofuro de sugoku ii aidea ga ukanda noni, wasurechatta no.
lines.ja: だって、昨日お風呂ですごくいいアイデアが浮かんだのに、忘れちゃったの。
lines.kana: だって、きのうおふろですごくいいあいであがうかんだのに、わすれちゃったの。
lines.english: But last night in the bath, a really good idea came to me, and now I've forgotten it!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, memo toranakatta no? watashi wa, aidea ga ukandara, sugu memo o toru you ni shiteru yo.
lines.ja: え、メモ取らなかったの？私は、アイデアが浮かんだら、すぐメモを取るようにしてるよ。
lines.kana: え、めもとらなかったの？わたしは、あいであがうかんだら、すぐめもをとるようにしてるよ。
lines.english: What, you didn't write it down? Whenever an idea comes to me, I make a point of writing it down right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ofuro de memo nanka toreru wake nai jan!
lines.ja: お風呂でメモなんか取れるわけないじゃん！
lines.kana: おふろでめもなんかとれるわけないじゃん！
lines.english: How am I supposed to take notes in the bath?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, chotto matte. kinou no yoru, ofuro no ato de denwa kureta yo ne?
lines.ja: あ、ちょっと待って。昨日の夜、お風呂のあとで電話くれたよね？
lines.kana: あ、ちょっとまって。きのうのよる、おふろのあとででんわくれたよね？
lines.english: Oh, hang on. Last night, you called me after your bath, didn't you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sou datta? tsukaretete, zenzen oboetenai.
lines.ja: え、そうだった？疲れてて、全然覚えてない。
lines.kana: え、そうだった？つかれてて、ぜんぜんおぼえてない。
lines.english: Huh, did I? I was so tired, I don't remember at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sugoi aidea ukanda! tte itteta kara, ichiou memo totta no. hora.
lines.ja: 「すごいアイデア浮かんだ！」って言ってたから、一応メモ取ったの。ほら。
lines.kana: 「すごいあいであうかんだ！」っていってたから、いちおうめもとったの。ほら。
lines.english: You said, "I've had an amazing idea!" so I wrote it down, just in case. Look.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: etto, atarashii aji no namae o, okyakusan ni kimete morau kyanpeen. sou sou, kore!
lines.ja: えっと、新しい味の名前を、お客さんに決めてもらうキャンペーン。そうそう、これ！
lines.kana: えっと、あたらしいあじのなまえを、おきゃくさんにきめてもらうきゃんぺーん。そうそう、これ！
lines.english: Let's see: "A campaign where customers choose the name of the new flavour." Yes, yes, this is it!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kore nara, kitto tanaka-san mo hanko oshite kureru shi, kekka mo daseru yo.
lines.ja: これなら、きっと田中さんもハンコ押してくれるし、結果も出せるよ。
lines.kana: これなら、きっとたなかさんもはんこおしてくれるし、けっかもだせるよ。
lines.english: With this, I bet Tanaka-san will give it his stamp, and we'll get results too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tanaka-san, aidea motte kimashita!
lines.ja: 田中さん、アイデア持ってきました！
lines.kana: たなかさん、あいであもってきました！
lines.english: Tanaka-san, I've brought you my idea!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: omoshiroi desu ne, kore. jaa, hanko o oshimasu ne.
lines.ja: 面白いですね、これ。じゃあ、ハンコを押しますね。
lines.kana: おもしろいですね、これ。じゃあ、はんこをおしますね。
lines.english: This is interesting. All right, I'll put my stamp on it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu! jitsu wa, kimura-san ga memo o totte kureta n desu.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます！実は、木村さんがメモを取ってくれたんです。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます！じつは、きむらさんがめもをとってくれたんです。
lines.english: Thank you! Actually, Kimura-san wrote it down for me.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. futari de, kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne.
lines.ja: そうですか。二人で、今度こそ結果を出してくださいね。
lines.kana: そうですか。ふたりで、こんどこそけっかをだしてくださいね。
lines.english: I see. Then the two of you, make sure you get results this time.

questions.english: What happened with Yuki's campaign idea?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki couldn't come up with anything, so Mai gave Tanaka-san one of her own ideas, and he approved it.
Yuki forgot the idea she had in the bath, but Mai had written it down when Yuki phoned her, and Tanaka-san approved it.
Yuki remembered her bath idea after a short break, but Tanaka-san said it needed more work before he'd stamp it.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Tanaka-san wants Yuki's campaign idea by the end of the day. Line 6: a great idea came to Yuki in the bath last night, but she has forgotten it. Lines 9-11: she phoned Mai after her bath, and Mai wrote the idea down just in case. Line 15: Tanaka-san likes it and presses his hanko on it, which means he approves. A is wrong: the idea was Yuki's own. Mai only wrote it down, and Yuki tells Tanaka-san so (line 16). C is wrong: Yuki never remembers it by herself. She reads it in Mai's notes (line 12), and Tanaka-san approves it on the spot.

questions.english: At lunch, Mai hands you her phone with a game on it and says, "kore, saikin hamatteru geemu. yatte miru?" You play a round. Tell her it really makes you think.
questions.ja: これ、最近ハマってるゲーム。やってみる？
questions.kana: これ、さいきんはまってるげーむ。やってみる？
questions.romaji: kore, saikin hamatteru geemu. yatte miru?
questions.answer: Say the game makes you think with atama o tsukau, casually atama tsukau, with kekkou or metcha for 'really': kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: このゲーム、結構頭使うね。
modelAnswers.english: This game really makes you think.

modelAnswers.romaji: muzukashii! kore, metcha atama tsukau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 難しい！これ、めっちゃ頭使うね。
modelAnswers.english: It's hard! This really gets your brain working.

questions.explanation: Yuki has been racking her brains since the morning (line 4, asa kara zutto atama tsukatteru), and Mai tells her she's overdoing it (line 5, atama tsukaisugi da yo). A game or a job that makes you think is one that 'uses your head': atama o tsukau, in casual speech usually without o. Don't mix it up with atama ga ii (be clever), or with ki o tsukau, which means being considerate. With a friend, casual is right.

questions.english: At the end, Tanaka-san tells Yuki and Mai what he wants from them this time. What did he say?
questions.ja: 田中さんは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: This time, make sure you get results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne

choices.english: This time, please go and receive the results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o moratte kudasai ne

choices.english: This time, please take the results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o totte kudasai ne

questions.explanation: Line 17: 'futari de, kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne'. Yuki used it in line 2 (kondo koso, kekka o dashitai desu ne), and Mai in line 13 (kekka mo daseru yo). Results you achieve are something you put out yourself: kekka o dasu. In line 1 Tanaka-san used the other verb, kekka ga demashita. There the results came out by themselves, meaning they were announced. B is wrong: morau means being handed something, so kekka o morau only fits getting a results sheet. C is wrong: toru works in ten o toru (get a score) and memo o toru, but results aren't 'taken'. You deliver them with dasu.

questions.english: Tanaka-san comes to your desk and says, "raishuu no kaigi, jikan ga kawatta node, ima iimasu ne." Ask him to wait a moment while you write it down.
questions.ja: 来週の会議、時間が変わったので、今言いますね。
questions.kana: らいしゅうのかいぎ、じかんがかわったので、いまいいますね。
questions.romaji: raishuu no kaigi, jikan ga kawatta node, ima iimasu ne.
questions.answer: Ask him to wait while you take a note, with memo o toru in polite form: chotto matte kudasai, memo o torimasu. He's your manager, so stay polite.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, chotto matte kudasai. ima memo o torimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ちょっと待ってください。今メモを取ります。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, just a moment, please. I'll write it down.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, memo o torimasu node, chotto matte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、メモを取りますので、ちょっと待ってください。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, let me take a note. Just a moment, please.

questions.explanation: Mai makes a point of noting ideas down the moment they come (line 7, sugu memo o toru you ni shiteru), and she wrote Yuki's idea down during the call (line 11, ichiou memo totta). Yuki tells Tanaka-san that Kimura-san took it down for her (line 16, memo o totte kureta). As in English, you 'take' notes: memo o toru. Memo suru means the same and is just as common. A note you leave for someone is memo o nokosu. With your manager, use torimasu and matte kudasai.

questions.english: Mai says everyone wants to get Tanaka-san something for his birthday, and asks you, "nee, nani ga ii to omou?" You've thought about it, but nothing comes to mind. Tell her.
questions.ja: 田中さんの誕生日、みんなで何かあげようって。ねえ、何がいいと思う？
questions.kana: たなかさんのたんじょうび、みんなでなにかあげようって。ねえ、なにがいいとおもう？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no tanjoubi, minna de nanika ageyou tte. nee, nani ga ii to omou?
questions.answer: Say no good idea comes to mind with aidea ga ukabu in the negative: zenzen ii aidea ukabanai. With Mai, casual is right.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, zenzen ii aidea ukabanai.
modelAnswers.ja: うーん、全然いいアイデア浮かばない。
modelAnswers.english: Hmm, I can't come up with any good ideas at all.

modelAnswers.romaji: nan darou. mada ii aidea ga ukabanai n da yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 何だろう。まだいいアイデアが浮かばないんだよね。
modelAnswers.english: Good question. No good idea has come to me yet.

questions.explanation: Yuki complains that no good idea comes to her (line 4, zenzen ii aidea ga ukabanai), though a great one came to her in the bath (line 6, ukanda). Ideas float up into your mind on their own, so the idea is the subject with ga: aidea ga ukabu, and casual speech often drops the ga. It is mostly heard in the negative, like this. Ukabu reports an idea coming, or not coming, to mind, as in sugoi aidea ukanda! (line 11). To offer an idea, 'I've got an idea!', people say ii kangae ga aru! or omoitsuita! With Mai, casual is right.

questions.english: Yuki brings her idea to Tanaka-san. What did he do?
questions.ja: 田中さんは、ユキのアイデアをどうしましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんは、ゆきのあいであをどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa, yuki no aidea o dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: He asked Yuki to put her own seal on it first, before he read it.
He gave it a fun 'good job' stamp, like a teacher, but hasn't decided yet.
He approved it: his seal on the plan means it can go ahead.

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'omoshiroi desu ne, kore. jaa, hanko o oshimasu ne.' In a Japanese office a manager approves a plan by pressing his personal seal (hanko) on it, so this means 'yes, go ahead'. He promised it in line 3 (ii aidea nara, sugu hanko o oshimasu kara), and Mai predicted it in line 13. A is wrong: nobody asks Yuki for her own seal. B is wrong: a fun rubber stamp, like a teacher's 'well done', is a sutanpu. A hanko is a personal seal, and you press it: hanko o osu.

edits.value: Line 4: 'jaa, mae no kafe de jikan tsubusou ka'. Kenji answers nanika tabenagara jikan tsubusou (line 5), and later mou hitotsu tabete, jikan tsubusou kana (line 16). Killing time is tsubusu, 'squash': you squash the empty time flat. B is a word-for-word copy of 'kill time'. Korosu is for killing living things, so jikan o korosu sounds like a murder plot. C is wrong: jikan o kakeru is putting time into something on purpose, like the doctor with each patient (line 2). Here they just want to fill a wait.
edits.why: 'Korosu is only for killing living things' is false: korosu has everyday figurative uses (iki o korosu, koe o korosu, aji o korosu). Dropping 'only' keeps the point without teaching something wrong.

edits.value: tanaka-san wa, yuki-san no aidea o dou shimashita ka?
edits.why: The narrator calls Tanaka-san -san but leaves Yuki's name bare in the same sentence. Every other question in the series says yuki-san, so this one should too.

edits.value: 田中さんは、ユキさんのアイデアをどうしましたか？
edits.why: Same fix as the romaji: ユキ becomes ユキさん, so both names get さん.

edits.value: たなかさんは、ゆきさんのあいであをどうしましたか？
edits.why: Same fix as the romaji: ゆき becomes ゆきさん, so the kana matches the ja.

91.title: Just a yawn
91.setting: A Saturday night outside a concert hall. Yuki has loved a singer for ten years and has just seen her live for the first time. Her old friend Kenta came along on her spare ticket, though he'd said he didn't know any of the songs.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, sugokatta! saigo no uta, torihada tatta!
lines.ja: ああ、すごかった！最後の歌、鳥肌立った！
lines.kana: ああ、すごかった！さいごのうた、とりはだたった！
lines.english: Wow, that was amazing! The last song gave me goosebumps!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakaru. hora, boku mo mada torihada tatteru.
lines.ja: わかる。ほら、僕もまだ鳥肌立ってる。
lines.kana: わかる。ほら、ぼくもまだとりはだたってる。
lines.english: I know. Look, I've still got goosebumps too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: desho? ano hito no uta, zenzen shiranai tte itteta noni.
lines.ja: でしょ？あの人の歌、全然知らないって言ってたのに。
lines.kana: でしょ？あのひとのうた、ぜんぜんしらないっていってたのに。
lines.english: Right? And you said you didn't know any of her songs.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, demo ii uta bakkari datta. yuki wa saisho kara naiteta ne.
lines.ja: うん、でもいい歌ばっかりだった。ユキは最初から泣いてたね。
lines.kana: うん、でもいいうたばっかりだった。ゆきはさいしょからないてたね。
lines.english: Yeah, but they were all great songs. You were crying from the very start.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: datte, juu nen matte, yatto aeta n da yo. mada jikkan wakanai.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: juu nen ka. jikkan wakanai no mo wakaru yo.
lines.ja: 十年か。実感湧かないのもわかるよ。
lines.kana: じゅうねんか。じっかんわかないのもわかるよ。
lines.english: Ten years, huh. I can see why it hasn't sunk in.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: are? kenta mo me akai yo. moshikashite, naiteta?
lines.ja: あれ？ケンタも目赤いよ。もしかして、泣いてた？
lines.kana: あれ？けんたもめあかいよ。もしかして、ないてた？
lines.english: Huh? Your eyes are red too, Kenta. Were you crying, by any chance?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: naitenai yo. chotto akubi shitara, namida deta dake.
lines.ja: 泣いてないよ。ちょっとあくびしたら、涙出ただけ。
lines.kana: ないてないよ。ちょっとあくびしたら、なみだでただけ。
lines.english: I wasn't crying. I yawned, and my eyes watered, that's all.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: saigo no uta de akubi? tsumaranakatta tte koto?
lines.ja: 最後の歌であくび？つまらなかったってこと？
lines.kana: さいごのうたであくび？つまらなかったってこと？

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: chigau chigau! nanka wakannai kedo, kyuu ni namida dete kita n da yo.
lines.ja: 違う違う！なんかわかんないけど、急に涙出てきたんだよ。
lines.kana: ちがうちがう！なんかわかんないけど、きゅうになみだでてきたんだよ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sore, naita tte iu n da yo.
lines.ja: それ、泣いたって言うんだよ。
lines.kana: それ、ないたっていうんだよ。
lines.english: That's called crying.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakatta yo. honne iu to, boku mo chotto naita.
lines.ja: わかったよ。本音言うと、僕もちょっと泣いた。
lines.kana: わかったよ。ほんねいうと、ぼくもちょっとないた。
lines.english: Fine. If I'm honest, I cried a bit too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: yappari! kenta made naku hodo yokatta n da ne.
lines.ja: やっぱり！ケンタまで泣くほどよかったんだね。
lines.kana: やっぱり！けんたまでなくほどよかったんだね。
lines.english: I knew it! So it was good enough to make even you cry.

lines.speaker: kenta

lines.kana: うん、ほんとによかった。ゆきは？すこしはじっかんわいてきた？
lines.english: Yeah, it was really good. What about you? Has it started to sink in?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, yatto waite kita. a, dame, mata namida desou.
lines.ja: うん、やっと湧いてきた。あ、だめ、また涙出そう。
lines.kana: うん、やっとわいてきた。あ、だめ、またなみだでそう。
lines.english: Yeah, it's finally sinking in. Oh no, I'm going to tear up again.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yamete yo. boku mo mata torihada tatte kita.
lines.ja: やめてよ。僕もまた鳥肌立ってきた。
lines.kana: やめてよ。ぼくもまたとりはだたってきた。
lines.english: Don't. Now I've got goosebumps again too.

questions.english: What happens after the concert?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta yawned through the last song because he didn't know it, and Yuki is upset that he found it boring.
Kenta blames a yawn for his teary eyes, but he ends up admitting the concert made him cry a little.
Kenta says he didn't cry, and Yuki believes him, since he didn't know any of the songs.

questions.explanation: Lines 7-8: Yuki sees that Kenta's eyes are red too and asks if he was crying. He says no, he just yawned and his eyes watered (akubi shitara, namida deta dake). In line 9 she asks if that means he was bored, and in line 10 he says no, the tears just suddenly came (kyuu ni namida dete kita). Yuki tells him that's called crying (line 11), and in line 12 he admits it: honne iu to, boku mo chotto naita. A is wrong: the yawn was only Kenta's excuse. He says chigau chigau! (line 10), and that the concert was really good (line 14). C is wrong: Yuki doesn't believe him (line 11), and he ends up admitting he cried.

questions.english: After lunch at the office, you give a big yawn and your eyes water. Mai, at the next desk, looks over and asks, "e, naiteru no? daijoubu?" Tell her you're not crying: your eyes just watered when you yawned.
questions.ja: え、泣いてるの？大丈夫？
questions.kana: え、ないてるの？だいじょうぶ？
questions.romaji: e, naiteru no? daijoubu?
questions.answer: Say you're not crying (naitenai yo), and that your eyes only watered because you yawned, with namida ga deru in the past: akubi shitara namida deta dake. In casual speech ga usually drops.

modelAnswers.romaji: naitenai yo. akubi shitara, namida deta dake.
modelAnswers.ja: 泣いてないよ。あくびしたら、涙出ただけ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm not crying. I yawned and my eyes watered, that's all.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, chigau chigau. akubi shitara, namida dete kichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、違う違う。あくびしたら、涙出てきちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: No, no, that's not it. I yawned, and my eyes started watering.

questions.explanation: Kenta uses it to deny crying: akubi shitara, namida deta dake (line 8). Then he gives himself away with kyuu ni namida dete kita (line 10, the tears just started coming), and at the end Yuki says mata namida desou (line 15, I'm going to tear up again). namida ga deru is tears coming out on their own: from a yawn, onions or laughing, or when something moves you. naku is crying from emotion. That's why Mai asks naiteru no?, and why Yuki tells Kenta sore, naita tte iu n da yo (line 11): tears because a song moved you count as crying. A yawn doesn't, so say naitenai and namida deta dake. With a friend like Mai, casual is right, and ga usually drops.

questions.english: Right after the concert, what does Yuki say about the last song?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、最後の歌について何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、さいごのうたについてなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, saigo no uta ni tsuite nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I got goosebumps from the last song! (morau: get, as in being given something)
choices.romaji: saigo no uta, torihada moratta!

choices.english: Goosebumps came out at the last song! (deru: come out, as tears do)
choices.romaji: saigo no uta, torihada deta!

choices.english: The last song gave me goosebumps!
choices.romaji: saigo no uta, torihada tatta!

questions.explanation: Line 1: 'saigo no uta, torihada tatta!' In Japanese, goosebumps stand up: torihada ga tatsu, and in casual speech ga usually drops. Kenta uses it twice: hora, boku mo mada torihada tatteru (line 2, look, I've still got goosebumps too) and boku mo mata torihada tatte kita (line 16). A is wrong: morau is 'get' as in being given something, so torihada moratta copies English 'got goosebumps' word for word. B is wrong: deru is the verb for tears (namida deta, line 8), but goosebumps don't come out, they stand up. Each reaction keeps its own verb: namida ga deru, torihada ga tatsu.

questions.english: You've just passed an exam you studied for all year. Your manager, Tanaka-san, comes over and says, "shiken, ukatta sou desu ne. omedetou gozaimasu." Thank him, and say it still hasn't sunk in.
questions.ja: 試験、受かったそうですね。おめでとうございます。
questions.kana: しけん、うかったそうですね。おめでとうございます。
questions.romaji: shiken, ukatta sou desu ne. omedetou gozaimasu.
questions.answer: Thank him (arigatou gozaimasu), then say it hasn't sunk in yet with jikkan ga waku in the negative: mada jikkan ga wakanai desu. With your manager, keep ga and add desu. With friends it's just mada jikkan wakanai.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. demo, mada jikkan ga wakanai desu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。でも、まだ実感が湧かないです。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. It still hasn't sunk in, though.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. jitsu wa, mada zenzen jikkan ga wakanai n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。実は、まだ全然実感が湧かないんです。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. Honestly, it hasn't sunk in at all yet.

questions.explanation: After finally seeing the singer, Yuki says mada jikkan wakanai (line 5, it still hasn't sunk in). Kenta answers jikkan wakanai no mo wakaru yo (line 6), and later asks sukoshi wa jikkan waite kita? (line 14, has it started to sink in?). jikkan is the real feel of something, and waku is a feeling welling up, so it's mostly said in the negative after big news like passing an exam, a new job or a baby. Don't say mada wakaranai or rikai shite nai, which sound as if you don't understand the news. Listen for one n: wakanai (doesn't well up, from waku) against wakannai (I don't get it), which Kenta says in line 10 (nanka wakannai kedo). With your manager, keep ga and add desu: mada jikkan ga wakanai desu.

92.title: Hatsumoude in April

lines.english: Wow, the blossoms are all out! It's been ages since I went cherry-blossom viewing.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kyonen wa futari tomo isogashikute, ohanami ikenakatta mon ne.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: nee, koko jinja desho? omikuji hiite ikou yo.

lines.kana: ねえ、ここじんじゃでしょ？おみくじひいていこうよ。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: omikuji wa, ii ya. hatsumoude no toki, daikyou datta kara.

lines.kana: おみくじは、いいや。はつもうでのとき、だいきょうだったから。
lines.english: I'll pass on the fortunes. At New Year I got very bad luck.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daikyou!? sonna no, honto ni haitteru n da.
lines.ja: 大凶！？そんなの、ほんとに入ってるんだ。
lines.kana: だいきょう！？そんなの、ほんとにはいってるんだ。
lines.english: Very bad luck!? So they really do put those in!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: haitteru yo. yuki to hatsumoude itte, yuki wa daikichi, kotchi wa daikyou.
lines.ja: 入ってるよ。ユキと初詣行って、ユキは大吉、こっちは大凶。
lines.kana: はいってるよ。ゆきとはつもうでいって、ゆきはだいきち、こっちはだいきょう。
lines.english: They do. I went to the shrine with Yuki at New Year. She got great luck, I got very bad luck.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ahaha, saiaku jan. demo boku nante, kotoshi mada hatsumoude ittenai yo.
lines.ja: あはは、最悪じゃん。でも僕なんて、今年まだ初詣行ってないよ。
lines.kana: あはは、さいあくじゃん。でもぼくなんて、ことしまだはつもうでいってないよ。
lines.english: Ha ha, that's the worst. But me, I haven't even made my New Year shrine visit yet.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, mou shigatsu da yo.
lines.ja: え、もう4月だよ。
lines.kana: え、もうしがつだよ。
lines.english: What? It's April already.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: dakara, kyou ga boku no hatsumoude. omikuji mo hikanakya.
lines.ja: だから、今日が僕の初詣。おみくじも引かなきゃ。
lines.kana: だから、きょうがぼくのはつもうで。おみくじもひかなきゃ。
lines.english: Exactly, so today's my first shrine visit of the year. I have to draw a fortune too.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ososugiru desho. maa, nikai mo daikyou wa denai ka.
lines.ja: 遅すぎるでしょ。まあ、二回も大凶は出ないか。
lines.kana: おそすぎるでしょ。まあ、にかいもだいきょうはでないか。
lines.english: That's way too late. Well, I can't get very bad luck twice, can I.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: hiita? jaa, issho ni miyou.
lines.ja: 引いた？じゃあ、一緒に見よう。
lines.kana: ひいた？じゃあ、いっしょにみよう。

lines.speaker: kenta

lines.speaker: sora

lines.ja: え、うそ。僕、大凶なんだけど。
lines.kana: え、うそ。ぼく、だいきょうなんだけど。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ahaha! shigatsu no hatsumoude wa, yappari dame da ne.
lines.ja: あはは！4月の初詣は、やっぱりだめだね。
lines.kana: あはは！しがつのはつもうでは、やっぱりだめだね。
lines.english: Ha ha! Guess a New Year visit in April doesn't count.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mou, kore musunde, hayaku ohanami ikou. yuki-tachi, matteru shi.
lines.ja: もう、これ結んで、早くお花見行こう。ユキたち、待ってるし。
lines.kana: もう、これむすんで、はやくおはなみいこう。ゆきたち、まってるし。
lines.english: Ugh. I'll tie this one up here, and let's get to the picnic. Yuki and the others are waiting.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. rainen wa chanto ichigatsu ni hatsumoude ikou ne.
lines.ja: うん。来年はちゃんと1月に初詣行こうね。
lines.kana: うん。らいねんはちゃんといちがつにはつもうでいこうね。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: iku. demo, omikuji wa mou hikanai.
lines.ja: 行く。でも、おみくじはもう引かない。
lines.kana: いく。でも、おみくじはもうひかない。
lines.english: I'm in. But I'm never drawing a fortune again.

questions.english: What happened at the shrine?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora drew great luck on his very late first shrine visit, and Kenta drew very bad luck for the second time.
Kenta drew great luck this time, but Sora, who called today his first shrine visit of the year, drew very bad luck.
Kenta wouldn't draw another fortune after his bad one at New Year, so only Sora drew one, and he got very bad luck.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-6: Kenta got daikyou (very bad luck) at New Year. Line 9: Sora hasn't been to a shrine yet this year, so today counts as his hatsumoude. Lines 10-13: Kenta draws again too and gets daikichi (great luck), and Sora gets daikyou. A swaps the two results; C is wrong because Kenta does draw again (line 10: nikai mo daikyou wa denai ka).

questions.english: A week before the picnic, Sora comes home and says, "hana, mou saiteru tte." Suggest going cherry-blossom viewing at the weekend.
questions.ja: 花、もう咲いてるって。
questions.kana: はな、もうさいてるって。
questions.romaji: hana, mou saiteru tte.
questions.answer: Invite him with ohanami ni iku in a let's-go form: ohanami ikou, or ohanami ikanai? (casual speech drops ni). Say ohanami, with the o-, not plain hanami.

modelAnswers.romaji: honto? jaa, shuumatsu ohanami ikou yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、週末お花見行こうよ。
modelAnswers.english: Really? Then let's go cherry-blossom viewing this weekend.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii ne. shuumatsu, yuki-tachi to ohanami ikanai?
modelAnswers.ja: いいね。週末、ユキたちとお花見行かない？
modelAnswers.english: Nice. Want to go cherry-blossom viewing with Yuki and the others this weekend?

questions.explanation: Lines 1, 2 and 15: ohanami iku no, ohanami ikenakatta, hayaku ohanami ikou. In speech it is nearly always ohanami, with the polite o-, and ni is usually dropped. ikou (let's go) and ikanai? (want to go?) are the everyday ways to invite. An ohanami is a picnic under the trees as much as looking at them.

questions.english: Right before Kenta points out that it's already April, what does Sora tell him?
questions.ja: ソラは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: He has never been to this shrine before.
He hasn't been cherry-blossom viewing yet this year.
He hasn't made his first shrine visit of the year yet.

questions.explanation: Line 7: kotoshi mada hatsumoude ittenai yo. hatsumoude is the year's first visit to a shrine or temple, normally made in the first days of January, which is why Kenta says it's already April and teases him about an April hatsumoude (line 14). A reads hatsu 'first' as 'first time ever'; B is ohanami, the outing they're on their way to, not the one Sora missed.

questions.english: It's 2 January and you've just got back from the shrine. Kenta asks, "hatsumoude, dou datta?" Tell him you drew a fortune slip, and what you got.
questions.ja: 初詣、どうだった？
questions.kana: はつもうで、どうだった？
questions.romaji: hatsumoude, dou datta?
questions.answer: Say you drew one with omikuji o hiku, usually omikuji hiita, or omikuji hiitara followed by the result (daikichi datta). Drawing a fortune is hiku, 'pull', not kaku.

modelAnswers.romaji: tanoshikatta yo. omikuji hiitara, daikichi datta!
modelAnswers.ja: 楽しかったよ。おみくじ引いたら、大吉だった！
modelAnswers.english: It was fun. I drew a fortune slip and got great luck!

modelAnswers.romaji: hito ga ippai datta kedo, omikuji hiita yo. daikichi!
modelAnswers.ja: 人がいっぱいだったけど、おみくじ引いたよ。大吉！
modelAnswers.english: It was packed, but I drew a fortune slip. Great luck!

questions.explanation: Lines 3, 9 and 17: omikuji hiite ikou yo, omikuji mo hikanakya, omikuji wa mou hikanai. Drawing lots or a fortune is hiku, 'pull', the same verb as kuji o hiku. English 'draw' pulls toward kaku, but that is drawing a picture, and omikuji o toru isn't said. It sounds like piano o hiku, but that is a different verb.

choices.english: Yuki put her hand up on purpose to impress Tanaka-san, and Mai helped her choose the best of her ideas.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Yuki only put her arms up because her shoulders hurt (te o ue ni ageta dake). Line 3: that was just when Tanaka-san asked anyone with a new idea to raise their hand. So now Yuki has to share an idea at next week's meeting (line 4), and she hasn't got one (line 6). Mai talks her through a stretch (lines 9-13), and with her eyes closed an idea comes to her (line 14): everyone doing the stretch before meetings (line 16). A is wrong: Yuki didn't mean to volunteer. She wasn't even listening (line 4), and she had no ideas at all (line 6). C swaps the two: Yuki is the one who put her hand up, and Mai leads the stretch.

questions.answer: Ask with te o ageru as a request: name the people, then te agete. Among friends it's iku hito, te agete! To a room of coworkers you can make it polite: ikitai hito wa, te o agete kudasai.

questions.explanation: Tanaka-san's request in line 3 is the classic shape: atarashii aidea ga aru hito wa, te o agete kudasai (anyone with a new idea, please raise your hand). Mai teases Yuki with it in line 17 (machigaete te o ageru hito, people who put their hand up by mistake). The same phrase covers putting your arms up to stretch (line 2, te o ue ni ageta, and line 9, te o ue ni agete). Among friends, o and kudasai drop: iku hito, te agete! Putting your hand back down is te o orosu. Careful with ni and a person: kodomo ni te o ageru means hitting a child.

questions.explanation: Line 9: 'jaa, me tojite'. Eyes take tojiru, the verb you also use for closing a book, an umbrella or an app. Yuki says it twice more: me tojiteru to, nechaisou (line 12, with my eyes closed I'll nod off) and me tojitetara, aidea ukanda (line 14). A is wrong: shimeru is for doors, windows and lids, so me o shimeru is the classic learner slip. B is wrong: kao agete means 'look up', with the same ageru as te o agete, but Mai asked Yuki to close her eyes first and then put her arms up (te o ue ni agete). In casual speech you'll also hear me tsubutte for 'close your eyes', and opening them again is me o akeru.

questions.english: It's the night before the meeting. Yuki's shoulders are up around her ears, and she says, "ashita no kaigi, dou shiyou. umaku hanaseru kana." Tell her to relax her shoulders, using chikara o nuku.

questions.answer: Tell her to relax with chikara o nuku as a request: chikara nuite, or kata no chikara nuite to name her shoulders. With a friend, casual is right and the o usually drops.

questions.explanation: Mai says it in line 7 (chotto chikara nuite), Yuki thought she already was (line 8, chikara nuiteru tsumori), Mai says it again in line 11, and Yuki's idea rests on it (line 16, chotto chikara nuku dake de, zenzen chigau yo). Nuku means pulling something out, so you pull the strength out of your body. The opposite is chikara o ireru (tense up), which Mai asks for first in line 11 (kata ni chikara irete), and a body that's tense is chikara ga haitteru (line 7). Kata no chikara o nuku also means 'stop trying so hard', which suits a friend worrying about a meeting. Rirakkusu shite is the other everyday way to say relax.
